content:
Artist Bermal Çem, who attended the European Jineolojî Conference as a representative of the cultural and artistic community, spoke to ANF about the discussions and workshops held during the conference and the impact of bringing together women from different peoples.




Bermal Çem said there was a profound sense of excitement at the conference, noting that numerous problems and possible solutions had been discussed over the three days. She said that the message Abdullah Öcalan sent to the conference had provided a powerful boost to the morale of both Kurdish women and the internationalist women in attendance.




‘Women's pursuit of freedom is shared’




Bermal Çem said the conference had discussed how Jineolojî could respond to the problems faced by Kurdish women living in all four parts of Kurdistan and abroad, as well as women from different peoples.




Çem said, “At a certain point, all women share common problems and a common pursuit of freedom. The oppression they experience in working life and within the family is the same, whether in the East or in Europe.




Jineolojî brings these women together. Discussions were held among women from different cultures and with different perspectives, centred on women's freedom and guided by women's philosophy and perspectives.”

title: Archaeological site believed to date back to the Abbasid period discovered in Babil
content:
The Press Office of Iraq’s Babil Governorate announced the discovery of an archaeological site in the Qasim district believed to date back to the Abbasid period, approximately 1,200 years ago.

According to a statement issued by the Press Office, the governor visited the site, examined the remains, assessed their historical significance, and discussed ways to preserve them.

The statement noted that the discovery could provide an opportunity to develop tourism in the district and promote its historical sites. It also highlighted the possibilities for developing the site as a tourist destination within the framework of laws governing the protection of existing archaeological heritage.

title: Who pays the price of peace?
content:
In his work 

The Old Regime and the Revolution

, Alexis de Tocqueville exposes one of the fundamental contradictions of the French Revolution: The monarchy had been overthrown, and the institutions of the old regime had been abolished, yet the centralist tradition of state domination over society persisted within the new order. The regime had changed, but the state’s power to determine social relations remained largely intact.




As Tocqueville demonstrates, therein lies a fundamental danger: Change can perpetuate existing power structures rather than overcome them.




From this perspective, the process currently underway in Turkey concerning the Kurdish question must also be examined. The decisive question is not merely whether the armed conflict will come to an end, but whether the historically entrenched relationship of domination from which this conflict emerged will also change.




After more than half a century of struggle, the Kurdish freedom movement has made historic decisions that fundamentally transform its armed strategy and organizational existence. These decisions cannot be explained by the naivety of a movement unaware of Turkey’s political realities. Throughout its long struggle, the Kurdish movement has come to understand the centralist nature of the state, its security-driven reflexes, and its resistance to democratization. content:

‘Restrictions cause unrest’




With the start of the new academic year in Syria, the organizations stated that Kurdish students who had previously received education in their mother tongue are now facing restrictions, with Kurdish-language instruction limited to just three hours.




The organizations said these restrictions have caused unrest among students and local communities and led to the cancellation of numerous classes.

Highlighting Syria’s national, linguistic, and religious diversity, the statement criticized the continuation of policies pursued under the former Assad regime. title: ÖHD documents environmental destruction on Mount Gabar
content:
The Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) has investigated the ongoing ecological destruction in the Gabar Mountains in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. A delegation from the Ecology Commission of the ÖHD’s provincial executive board and its local branch documented the impact of large-scale deforestation and intensive oil extraction on the ground. The findings of the investigation are expected to be published in a report in the coming days.




ÖHD lawyer Hülya Yıldırım regards the activities on Mount Gabar not as an isolated case of environmental destruction, but as part of the war and security policies pursued in Kurdistan for decades. She noted that forests are also being cleared in the neighboring mountainous regions of Besta and Cudi, while fires are destroying large areas of land and natural habitats are being damaged by mining operations and environmentally harmful industrial facilities.




“There are now oil wells and extraction facilities in virtually every corner of Mount Gabar. As a result, the mountain is literally being blasted apart. The Tigris River is being polluted by oil leaks and petroleum waste,” said Yıldırım, a member of the ÖHD Ecology Commission.

title: Koçyiğit: We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice
content:
The Turkish government plans to increase spending on defense and the arms industry by more than 60 percent in 2027. Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, deputy parliamentary group chair of the DEM Party, criticized these budget priorities in light of the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process. While billions are being allocated to the military and security apparatus, funding remains insufficient for social welfare, healthcare, and education, she underlined.




At a press conference in the Turkish Parliament in Ankara, Koçyiğit put the planned defense expenditure for 2027 at 3.454 trillion Turkish lira (nearly 62.1 billion euros). This represents an increase of 60.28 percent compared to the 2026 budget. The planned increase, she argued, contradicts political statements about a peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question.




“We would have liked to see a substantial portion of the budget actually allocated to improving the well-being of the population and covering healthcare and education costs,” the DEM Party politician stated.




‘We want to see peace in the budget, in language, and in practice’




Koçyiğit called for the peace process not to be limited to political statements and negotiations. She stated that a departure from decades of conflict-driven policies must also be reflected in the state’s economic priorities.

title: “Şahiya Hebûn û Azadî” events kicks off in Germany
content:
The opening of the “Şahiya Hebûn û Azadî” events, organized in Stuttgart and the nearby cities of Reutlingen and Tübingen, has taken place.




The event, which featured cultural programs and political assessments, addressed the peace and democratic society process currently on the agenda of the Kurdish people.




The program attracted a large audience and featured performances by artists Simar, Narinxan, and Çiwo Bakur.




Speaking at the event, politician Faysal Sarıyıldız drew attention to the current stage of the process and the steps that need to be taken in the period ahead.




Sarıyıldız emphasized the need to embrace the process, take part in the communes to be established, and strengthen social organization. He also highlighted the importance of expanding democratic organization and continuing political activities.




Following the speeches, artists Simar, Narinxan, and Kurdish rap artist Çiwo Bakur took to the stage. The program, which included musical performances and cultural activities, concluded amid strong interest from participants.




As part of “Şahiya Hebûn û Azadî,” various cultural events and commemorative programs will be held over the coming month in Stuttgart and surrounding cities. Different programs are planned for each weekend, with events also expected to continue in other cities across the region.

title: How will we build an understanding of democratic integration?
content:
Integration represents a transitional process for achieving peace and reconciliation. Knowing that every grain of these lands, stones, trees, and flowers belongs to us, that this is our country, we will work hard to make our country more beautiful.




As freedom fighters, we will carry out pioneering work in every sphere, from the children and mothers of this country to its nature, production, technology, and all aspects of life. Until now, we have defended our honour, will, existence, and identity with weapons in this country. Now, too, we will protect and develop everything, from its economy and ecology to its water and air.




We will bring this country to a leading position in the Middle East as well. We will raise, educate, and develop the consciousness of simple and humble people on the basis of truth and beauty. In short, we dreamed of a moral and political society. We see the practical steps towards realizing this dream and the foundations of the democratic society paradigm as very strong. This paradigm has inspired the world. If we are to build society in our country on the basis of this paradigm, we must place truth, beauty, simplicity, politics, morality, and aesthetics at the centre of our efforts.

title: Families demand reconstruction of destroyed guerrilla cemeteries in Şırnak
content:
Following the process initiated by the Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, many cemeteries in Kurdistan that had been prohibited for years were visited for the first time. HPG and YJA Star guerrillas were buried there, but have been demolished. Gravestones had been rendered unrecognizable by excavators, damaged in aerial attacks, and, in some cases, buried in pits. In Şirnak (Şirnex), where such attacks have become systematic, families are calling for the cemeteries to be rebuilt and access routes reopened.







 







The Cuma Bilika and Binevş Edessa Martyrs’ Cemetery on Mount Cûdî was bombed and destroyed in 2015; its surrounding wall, mosque, and guesthouse were also damaged. The cemetery, which could not be visited for years on the grounds that it was in a military security zone, was visited on 2 August 2026, for the first time in 11 years. On 11 October it was discovered that the gravestones had been buried together in a pit. At the cemetery, the family of Cihan Zilan (Hatice Erbağa), who fell as a martyr in 2006, found the grave they had been searching for over the years.




The Martyr Binevş Cemetery in the village of Basret on Mount Gabar was also targeted in the attacks. It was learned that the cemetery, built between 2010 and 2014, had been damaged and that numerous gravestones bearing the names of those who had fallen as martyrs had been broken.

content:
The Arîn Student Association opened in İskender Paşa neighbourhood in Istanbul's Fatih district, established through the initiative of university students. The association attracted considerable interest from students, young people and local residents within hours of opening.




The opening ceremony began with traditional clothing, slogans, applause and halay dances. Feleknaz Karabaş, a member of the Istanbul Peace Mothers' Assembly, was the first to speak. Karabaş said, “It is a source of pride to see you young people protecting your language and culture. Without you, we are incomplete. Language, culture and art are the foundations of a people's existence. Let us protect our existence.”







 







Students reject impositions and come together to build an alternative




Arîn Student Association member Melisa Çelik then read out a press statement. Çelik highlighted the lack of spaces where students can express themselves freely, saying: “Educational institutions, which should contribute to the qualitative development of society in cultural, scientific and social fields, are instead seeking to create obedient and passive masses serving the interests of those in power in particular and capitalist modernity in general. As students, we reject these impositions and have come together here today to develop an alternative.”

Referring to their meetings with Iraqi state officials, Hadi Elyas said: “Our talks with senior security and military officials began in February. The aim was to reach a sound and secure agreement on the integration of our forces, institutions, and community into the Iraqi state system. This is also a process that serves Iraq’s sovereignty. We take this matter very seriously. A formal and legitimate framework is also needed to resolve the other problems facing Shengal. Resolving this issue is a first step toward broader solutions.”




Emphasizing that the problems in Shengal cannot be reduced to security concerns alone, Hadi Elyas continued: “Although security is a very important issue, there are other fundamental matters that need to be addressed, such as the return of displaced people, compensation for citizens, the reconstruction of residential areas, and locating missing persons and those held captive by ISIS. title: DEM Party instructs its municipalities to apply to ministry for Kurdish language units
content:
The DEM Party is advancing efforts to institutionalize Kurdish language promotion within municipal administrations. The party’s Council for Democratic Local Governments has instructed municipalities under its administration to apply to Turkey’s Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change for the establishment of independent administrative units dedicated to the preservation and promotion of languages. A corresponding circular has been sent to the municipalities.




The initiative is based on resolutions adopted at the “Conference of Democratic Local Governments” held on June 8 and 9. Under these resolutions, metropolitan municipalities are to establish dedicated departments for the preservation and development of languages. Corresponding directorates are planned for other city, district, and municipal administrations.




Legal obstacles to establishing new departments




During its review of the legal and administrative requirements, the DEM Party found that existing regulations make it difficult to establish these administrative units directly. The Council for Democratic Local Governments therefore developed an alternative approach.

title: PJAK spokesperson Awdanan: Opponents of democracy fear integration
content:
Rêbwar Awdanan, spokesperson for the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), issued a message targeting individuals and groups opposed to PJAK and pro-democracy forces. Awdanan addressed a range of issues, from the idea of democratic integration and society’s self-governance to the slogan “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” and the achievements of the Kurdish people.




Oppnonents of democracy are thinking about getting a share of power




Stating that opponents of democracy are uncomfortable with the people’s democratic outlook, Rêbwar Awdanan said: “They are opponents of democracy and are extremely sensitive to the outlook embraced by the people. That is why we speak about democracy every day. They think only about the share of power they can secure for themselves. The establishment of a decentralized democratic republic and Iran’s diversity are sources of fear and terror for them. That is why we challenge this mindset every day and speak about a Democratic Republic of Iran.”




Democratic integration exposes fascist ideas




Criticizing groups opposed to the idea of democratic integration, Awdanan said this approach exposes their views and their attitudes toward peoples, continuing: “They are afraid of the idea of democratic integration because they are slaves to a thousand masters, and democratic integration exposes their fascist ideas and hostility toward peoples. title: ‘Temporary’ for 41 years: Turkey’s village guard system
content:
When Turkey introduced the system of so-called temporary village guards on March 26, 1985, it was officially intended as a time-limited “security measure.” Forty-one years later, the armed structure remains in place. Tens of thousands of village guards are still on duty, even though the PKK has ended its phase of armed struggle and the Peace and Democratic Society Process now has a legal framework.




This brings a question back into focus: How should the armed civilian apparatus that the Turkish state built up over decades during its war against the Kurdish freedom movement be dismantled?




According to the Turkish Ministry of Interior, 48,365 village guards were still on duty as of October 31, 2025. Their number is likely to have since fallen to approximately 47,000–48,000 due to retirements and the suspension of new recruitment.




The system, originally established as a temporary arrangement, thus remains part of the state security apparatus in Kurdistan more than four decades later.




A temporary measure becomes a permanent institution




The legal basis was established in 1985 through an amendment to Article 74 of the Village Law. Initially introduced in 22 provinces, the village guard system was intended to support military operations against the PKK by recruiting armed forces from the local population. title: KJK calls for action for Varisheh Moradi: Do not remain silent against executions
content:
The Coordination of the Kurdistan Women’s Communities (KJK) issued a written statement regarding the Iranian regime’s renewed death sentence against Kurdish activist Varisheh Moradi.




Condemning the Iranian regime’s actions, the KJK stated that women would defeat the policy of executions through their struggle for freedom and solidarity and organize in all areas of life to gain a voice and secure their rights.




‘Varisheh Moradi has represented the will of all imprisoned and freedom-loving women’




KJK recalled that Varisheh Moradi was arrested by the Iranian regime on August 1, 2023, and sentenced to death in November 2024. The sentence was overturned by a court in 2025.




The statement noted that Moradi had made her voice heard by women and people around the world through her stance and resistance since the day of her arrest. By refusing to appear in court, she took an open and uncompromising stand against the state’s unlawful practices and injustices, it said.




The statement continued: “Through her resistance and determination, Varisheh Moradi has represented the will of all imprisoned and freedom-loving women held in the Iranian regime’s prisons. In doing so, she has helped advance the struggle of women in prison in a more organized manner.”

title: Attack on martyrs’ cemetery in Aleppo sparks protests in Rojava
content:
An attack on the martyrs’ cemetery in the Sheikh Maqsoud (Şêxmeqsûd) neighborhood of Aleppo has sparked protests in several cities across Rojava. Unidentified individuals attacked the cemetery and desecrated graves, particularly that of YPG commander Şervan Heleb. The Councils of Martyrs’ Families condemned the attack in a joint statement and demanded an immediate investigation into the incident and the prosecution of those responsible.




The statement was read publicly in Qamişlo, Hesekê, Girkê Legê, Çilaxa, Amûdê, Tirbespiyê, Dêrik, and Dirbêsiyê, among other locations. Relatives of fallen fighters and representatives of civil society organizations and institutions participated in the gatherings. The statements were delivered in both Kurdish and Arabic.




‘A direct attack on the dignity of our people’




In their statement, the Councils of Martyrs’ Families described the attack on the cemetery in Sheikh Maqsoud as a deliberate violation of the memory of the martyrs.




“Attacking the resting places and images of the martyrs is not simply an attack on a physical structure. It is a direct attack on our sacred values and the dignity of our people,” the statement read.




The families emphasized that this was not an isolated incident. They recalled that graves and memorial portraits had previously been targeted at the martyrs’ cemetery in Shaddadi (Şedadê) and in other cit

title: IRGC intensifies drone attacks and artillery shelling in Kurdistan
content:
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has intensified its military operations in Kurdistan, launching drone attacks and artillery shelling against mountainous areas near the village of Goyleh in Marivan County, Kurdistan Province, according to sources who spoke to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN).




A resident of Goyleh told KHRN that IRGC forces arrived in the area at approximately 6:30 a.m. on Sunday, 18 October 2026, in a military convoy equipped with artillery and drones, taking up positions around the village in the Sarshiv region.




The source said the forces first struck the nearby mountainous area of Dasht-e Mil with two one-way attack drones before subjecting the area to heavy artillery shelling.




No reports of armed clashes in the area had been received at the time of publication.




The latest attacks follow similar military operations in other parts of Kurdistan in recent days.




The IRGC previously targeted the mountainous Shaho region, between Sarvabad in Kurdistan Province and Paveh in Kermanshah Province, as well as the Kalatarzan area of Sanandaj County, with one-way attack drones and artillery fire.




In a statement on Saturday, the Command of the East Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) warned that it would fully exercise its right to self-defense if the attacks continued.

title: Kira Legerhausen: We have entered a new phase of building society
content:
After twelve years of Jineolojî work in Europe, the Kurdish women’s science is undergoing a reorientation. Existing methods are to be reviewed, research projects more closely linked to everyday social life, and new forms of communal organization developed. Kira Legerhausen of the Jineolojî Academy spoke to ANF about these issues on the sidelines of the European Jineolojî Conference in Haelen, the Netherlands. Her focus is on women’s living conditions, overcoming patriarchal relationships, and exploring how scientific knowledge can contribute to tangible social change.




“We have entered an important phase. It is a process of rebuilding, change, and transformation,” Legerhausen explained. Over the past twelve years, various forms of work have emerged in Germany, France, Spain, and other European countries. Conferences in Cologne, Paris, and Stockholm have helped bring together women from different societies and political movements. The task now is to draw lessons from these experiences, she noted.




“We want to both expand and deepen our work,” Legerhausen said. This includes critically reviewing existing research approaches and organizational structures and developing new forms of social cooperation.

title: Four DEM Party Youth Council members detained in Mardin
content:
Turkish police detained four members of the DEM Party’s Youth Council during house raids in the central district of Artuklu in Mardin on Friday evening. Those detained were identified as Mahsum Çalhan, Serhat Akpınar, Abdulkadir Elmas, and Bilal Elmas.

The detentions were reportedly linked to the hanging of a banner. The four young men were taken to police headquarters. After interrogations at the police headquarters, they were brought before the prosecutor’s office on allegations of “making propaganda for an illegal organization.”

The four young men were then released under judicial supervision.

title: Final declaration of the European Jineolojî Conference: We weave the path from words to life
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference was held from 15 to 18 October 2026 in the city of Haelen, the Netherlands.




The conference, which saw the participation of around 150 delegates from 10 countries under the slogan “Building a Communal Free Life with Jineolojî” (“Bi Jineolojî ber bi Avakirina Jiyana Komunal û Azad”), concluded with the reading of its final declaration and a closing speech.




The final declaration of the European Jineolojî Conference reads as follows:




“We came together, drawing from different geographies, languages, and women’s memories. We gathered to remember the stories that others seek to make us forget, to build bridges between our lives that have been torn apart, and to weave the path to freedom together. In the light of Jineolojî, we reaffirm our determination to redefine women’s existence in its historical and social reality and to expand the knowledge of a free life.




The crisis we are living through is also a crisis of people being severed from their own truth and social bonds. When women’s memory is erased, the memory of history is diminished; when their labour is made invisible, the foundations of life remain obscured; when their voices are suppressed, society becomes alienated from its own truth. Jineolojî aims to overcome this rupture by bringing women’s history, knowledge, and social existence into the light. For social freedom cannot b

title: Aze Ronecan: Jineolojî made me question what kind of society I want to build
content:
Aze Ronecan said that she first encountered Jineolojî at a youth camp held in Europe, and added: “Until then, I had heard about Jineolojî from feminist and transfeminist circles in Europe, but I had never studied its ideology in depth. To me, it seemed more like an experience specific to Kurdish women. However, during this training, I realised that Jineolojî is a paradigm that speaks to all women around the world.”







 







I want to build a communal way of life




Aze Ronecan said she had grown up in Milan within a liberal and positivist worldview, and added that creating a communal way of life alongside other women remains an important area of struggle for her. “Understanding how we can struggle together with other women and how we can build a commune is still difficult for me. I haven’t found a solution yet, but I want to achieve this. That is also why I am here,” Aze Ronecan said.




I began questioning the roots of problems thanks to Jineolojî




Aze Ronecan said that Jineolojî had changed the way she approached events and issues. “Through Jineolojî, I began investigating the roots of problems. I ask myself ‘Why?’ more often. I try to understand how and why we act in certain ways. I try to be more patient and to listen more closely to other women,” she said.

title: Rezan Gezer: The government views releases from prison as a political concession
content:
As thousands of political prisoners held in prisons are expected to be released under the framework law, the government’s failure to take concrete steps and the prolonged process have intensified debate over human rights violations in prisons.




Unlawful decisions by the Prison Administration and Observation Boards are preventing the release of political prisoners, particularly those who are ill. Meanwhile, prison authorities continue practices aimed at stripping prisoners of rights they have already acquired.




Rezan Gezer, a member of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), spoke to ANF about the current situation in prisons and the impact of the Peace and Democratic Society Process on prisoners.




The transfer and release of prisoners keep being postponed




Stating that unlawful practices continue in prisons, Rezan Gezer said that, according to the latest information available to them, there are approximately 100 ill prisoners.




Gezer said: “Human rights violations in prisons are continuing. Problems related to healthcare conditions and unlawful practices persist. title: Ecocide and the communal solution
content:
The world is truly at an impasse. From global warming to the extinction of animal and plant species every single day, we find ourselves in the midst of an increasingly bleak picture. Moreover, this crisis has roots far too deep and a history far too long to be resolved through temporary measures such as picking up litter or switching off the lights. The destruction of nature taking place before our very eyes has now spiralled out of control. Why? Because we are confronted with a greedy system that sees the world solely as a source of profit, concentrates power in a single centre and seeks to exploit absolutely everything.




This is why we must first dismantle the mentality that has whispered to humanity for centuries: "You are the master of nature. It belongs to you, and you can plunder it as you please." We are not beings detached from nature or independent of it. On the contrary, we have emerged from nature, drawn our very life from it and become the part of nature that has found its voice and developed consciousness.




So when did things go wrong? The rupture began when classes, mechanisms of oppression and hierarchies based on the belief that "I am superior to you" emerged among human beings. That was when humanity became alienated from its own essence. The desire of human beings to oppress one another gradually turned into a ruthless obsession with exploiting nature. T

title: Mother Hediye: My son was a partisan
content:
The history of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement is also the history of one of the longest-running resistance struggles in the world. The resistance movement, which emerged in response to more than a century of genocidal attacks against the Kurdish people, transformed every aspect of their lives, enabling them to shake off the weight of oppression and become a people capable of developing and advancing their own struggle.




The 1990s hold a particularly important place in the history of the Freedom Movement. A people who had been increasingly enslaved by repression, special warfare policies and attempts at assimilation rose up in a powerful rebellion during that decade, paving the way for the defeat of the attacks that had long been inflicted upon the Kurds.




The People's Liberation Army of Kurdistan (ARGK) became a genuine people's army in the 1990s. Thousands of young Kurds rejected the poverty and the life within the established system imposed upon them, leaving their villages and cities to join the ranks of the ARGK.




Salih (Edip Karabay) was one of these thousands of young people. An ordinary Kurdish villager, Salih encountered the Freedom Movement in Istanbul, where he had gone to attend high school. title: Şêxo: Residents returning to Afrin and Serêkaniyê are not getting their homes and properties back
content:
With the integration agreement signed on 29 January 2026, between the Syrian Interim Government and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), Syria entered a new phase. The agreement aimed to reorganize the security apparatus, incorporate local administrations into the central system while preserving them, ensure the safe return of displaced people to their homes, and guarantee the fundamental rights of all communities.




However, over the period that followed, serious discrepancies emerged between the provisions of the agreement and their implementation on the ground. The agreement required that residents forcibly displaced from Afrin (Efrîn), Serêkaniyê, Shehba, and Girê Spî be enabled to return home safely, and that the Syrian Interim Government ensure the evacuation of homes occupied by armed groups and people who had arrived from other cities.




At this stage, tens of thousands of people have returned to Afrin, while more than 2,000 people have returned to their homes in Serêkaniyê in recent days. However, it has been reported that armed groups and some Arab families who settled in these homes have refused to vacate properties belonging to the returning residents.




Îbrahîm Şêxo, spokesperson for the Afrin Human Rights Organization, spoke to ANF about the problems faced by families returning to their homes.

title: The olive tree: The silent sage of time
content:
The olive tree is nature’s ancient sage, a symbol of patience and immortality. Its silvery leaves reach towards the sky, whispering in the wind like a timeless tale. Its roots carry patience deep into history, while its trunk defies the passage of time. Its fruit embodies the fertility of the earth, a golden gift from nature.




The olive tree is a symbol of resilience and peace, capable of taking root even in poor soil and surviving for centuries. Its olives and oil offer humanity nourishment, healing and abundance, while its leaves seem to hold the pages of history. Every branch tells a different story.




Each leaf carries the wisdom of the past into the present, while every ring whispers of the years it has silently witnessed. Carrying the earth’s abundance through its veins, this tree embodies a resistance that does not yield to the passing seasons but grows ever stronger, reflecting the enduring presence of peace and hope. It is a silent vow of patience whispered to the earth and peace written across the sky.




The olive tree is one of nature’s greatest wonders. Its ability to live for thousands of years, its trunk twisting like a sculpture and its capacity to flourish again despite every drought are testament to its extraordinary will to survive.

title: Dilar Dirik: We are discussing how we can transform life through Jineolojî
content:
Speaking to ANF, Dilar Dirik, who attended the European Jineolojî Conference held in Haelen, the Netherlands, under the theme “The Role of Jineolojî in Building Democratic and Communal Life,” assessed the development of Jineolojî in Europe, its relationship with the women’s liberation struggle, and the role it needs to assume in the new period.




Stating that Jineolojî studies in Europe reached an important milestone with the first conference, held in Cologne in 2014, Dilar Dirik said that over the past 12 years, both the scope of the work and the nature of the discussions had changed.




Dilar Dirik explained that initially the focus was on defining Jineolojî and explaining its aims and mission. Today, however, discussions have moved beyond theory and are increasingly focused on concrete methods for transforming social life.







 







An important transformation has taken place since 2014




Drawing attention to the history of Jineolojî studies in Europe, Dilar Dirik said that the first conference, held in Cologne in 2014, marked an important beginning. She said: “Looking at the history of Jineolojî studies in Europe, we can say that many changes have taken place, particularly since the first Jineolojî Conference held in Cologne in 2014. At the beginning, the main aim was largely to explain what Jineolojî was, define it, and set out its aims, role, and mission.

title: Ronda Tayfur: Jineolojî enables us to look at problems from different perspectives
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference, held in Haelen, the Netherlands, and titled “The Role of Jineolojî in Building a Democratic and Communal Life,” brought together participants from across Europe. Speaking to ANF, Ronda Tayfur discussed how she came to know Jineolojî, her experiences in the women’s freedom struggle, and the discussions held at the conference.




Tayfur, who works within the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Switzerland, emphasized that Jineolojî is not merely a theoretical field but offers a perspective that helps people approach the problems they encounter in everyday life from different angles.




I first encountered Jineolojî in 2014




Tayfur said she first encountered Jineolojî in 2014, while studying at university in Istanbul. The workshops and discussions she attended during that period helped her develop a new perspective. “I first encountered Jineolojî in 2014, when I was studying at university in Istanbul. It was something entirely new to me. That year was when I first engaged with Jineolojî, attended its workshops, and took part in discussions.




Because of the environment we lived in and the geography in which we grew up, we had always been interested in women’s freedom and gender consciousness. But Jineolojî encouraged us to look at things from a different perspective. That is what drew me to it.”

title: Jineolojî must connect with society’s needs, say women at Haelen conference
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference titled “The Role of Jineolojî in Building a Democratic and Communal Life,” is being held in Haelen. The third session focused on “Socializing Knowledge and Decolonizing Science.” Participants discussed collective learning, educational methods, knowledge production and the role of women’s knowledge in building a democratic society.




Presentations were given by Jineolojî Committee members Yasemin Anday and Nûjîn Derya, and Jînda Amed of the European Kurdish Women’s Movement (TJK-E). Topics included educational experiences, research, the social role of academies and strengthening local organization.




Education was the foundation for building a new human being




Reflecting on the Kurdish Freedom Movement’s educational experience and the development of Jineolojî from this legacy, Jînda Amed said education had been a central focus since the movement’s beginnings. Initiated with limited resources under the leadership of Haki Karer and Kemal Pir, educational activities gradually expanded and adopted new methods. Their aim was not only to transmit knowledge but also to shape people’s identities and personalities.




She said education emphasized ethics, morality, love for humanity and nature, women’s liberation and overcoming feudal influences. “Jineolojî, too, grew out of these values. It is their product,” she stated.

author: Unknown
title: Whereabouts of man summoned by Iranian Revolutionary Guards remain unknown
content:
A 40-year-old man has been detained in the city of Piranshahr in East Kurdistan (Rojhilat) after being summoned by the intelligence service of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). His whereabouts have remained unknown since his detention. The man, Ahmad Mostafanejad, has been denied access to legal counsel and contact with his family.




According to the human rights organization Kolbarnews, Mostafanejad was summoned by telephone to the Revolutionary Guards’ intelligence department in Piranshahr on Wednesday, October 14. After complying with the summons, he was detained and taken to an undisclosed location.




No information has yet emerged about the reasons for his detention or any possible charges against him. His health condition and detention conditions also remain unknown. Iranian authorities have neither disclosed his whereabouts nor allowed him to contact his family.

title: Jineolojî Conference: Women’s liberation must become a force for shaping society
content:
How can the ideology of women’s liberation become a politically effective force in society? This question was at the center of the second day of the European Jineolojî Conference in Haelen, the Netherlands. Around 150 delegates discussed building a democratic and communal society, overcoming hierarchical forms of organization, and integrating Jineolojî more deeply into everyday social life. Shortcomings in previous work were also openly addressed.




Alongside Jineolojî activists, the conference brought together representatives of women’s councils, communes, cultural and faith communities, media outlets, and civil society organizations, as well as mothers. The session on the transition from the ideology of women’s liberation to organized political practice featured contributions from scholar Dilar Dirik, Meral Çiçek of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E), and Elif Kaya of the Jineolojî Academy.




Dilar Dirik: ‘Transformation requires courage’




Dilar Dirik raised the question of the internal conditions necessary for social transformation. She argued that simply continuing existing activities or establishing new organizational structures was not enough. Instead, deeply entrenched ways of thinking, taboos, and patriarchal patterns of behavior must also be overcome, she underlined.

title: Saturday Mothers demand answers about the disappearance of Fehmi Tosun
content:
At their 1,125th vigil in Galatasaray Square in Istanbul, the Saturday Mothers commemorated Fehmi Tosun, a Kurd from Lice who was abducted in front of his family 31 years ago and has been missing ever since. Holding photographs of their relatives and red carnations, participants once again demanded that cases of enforced disappearance be investigated and those responsible brought to justice.




The gathering focused on the still-unresolved abduction of Tosun, who was 35 years old and a father of five at the time. Ikbal Eren, whose brother Hayrettin Eren also disappeared while in police custody, recalled that numerous people had witnessed Tosun’s abduction and that his family had concrete information about the perpetrators.




On the evening of October 19, 1995, three armed men in civilian clothes brought Tosun to his home in Istanbul’s Avcılar district in a white Renault. When he saw his wife and five children, he shouted, “They are going to kill me!” Before his family could reach him, he was forcibly dragged into the vehicle and taken away.




His wife, Hanım Tosun, immediately reported the abduction to the police and provided officers with the vehicle’s license plate number. Although the officers checked the license plate and made phone calls, they eventually stated that there was nothing they could do. The authorities later denied having taken Tosun into custody. author: Unknown
title: Deforestation on Mount Dorşîn in Amed countryside expands
content:
Deforestation on Mount Dorşîn in the Kulp district of Amed (Diyarbakır) province continues to advance. The tree felling has now spread to a new area near the hamlet of Zimak in the rural part of Eskar.




The affected area has been closed to the public on “security” grounds. While access is strictly controlled, the felled trees are transported out without obstruction. Trucks carry the timber through military checkpoints all the way to Amed.




According to information from the region, at least two truckloads of timber are transported away every day. The trees, felled by village guards under the supervision of the Turkish military, are transported through military checkpoints to Amed.

title: YRK: We will exercise our right to self-defense against any attack targeting our people and forces
content:
The Command of the East Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) issued a written statement regarding the latest attacks by the Iranian regime on the Shaho region. The YRK warned that it would fully exercise its right to self-defense if the attacks continued.




The YRK Command’s statement on Saturday reads as follows:




“Recently, our forces have once again become targets of attacks by the Iranian regime. We are sharing information about each attack to ensure that the public is informed of the facts. As we have stated before, we reiterate once again: We will exercise our right to self-defense against any attack targeting our people and our forces.




Since October 13, the Iranian regime has deployed a large force of Revolutionary Guards (Pasdaran), along with heavy weapons and kamikaze (explosive-laden) unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), to the Shaho region. On October 13, the enemy bombed and shelled the Qilbê Plain area using heavy weapons and kamikaze drones.




Furthermore, in the early hours of October 15, the Kela Terzan area was attacked by four UAVs, followed by further bombardment by Revolutionary Guard forces that continued until noon. The regime has increased the number of troops in the region, indicating its intention to continue military operations and attacks against our forces in this area.

title: Franco Cavalli: The left’s weakness fuels the far right’s rise
content:
The rise of far-right and racist movements across Europe is deepening concerns about the continent's political future. The growing strength of Alternative for Germany (AfD), the increasing political influence of the far right in France and the policies of Giorgia Meloni's government in Italy have reignited debates about Europe's future. The economic crisis, the so-called “migration crisis”, growing inequalities and social discontent fuelled by neoliberal policies are among the key factors driving the rise of the far right.




What dynamics lie behind the rise of the far right in Europe? Why have left-wing movements been unable to offer a strong alternative? What is the relationship between the crisis of capitalism and fascist tendencies? We put these questions to Swiss politician and physician Franco Cavalli. Cavalli spoke to ANF about developments in Europe, drawing particular attention to the dangers posed by Germany's rearmament policies and the rise of the AfD. He said the left had largely embraced neoliberal policies over the past three decades, arguing that the rise of the far right was driven not only by the economic crisis but also by the ideological and political weakness of the left.




How do you assess the rise of the far right in Europe? Is it possible to describe what we are witnessing today as the threat of a new form of fascism?

content:
Seven workshops were held at the European Jineolojî Conference, organised under the slogan “Building a free communal life through Jineolojî”.




Ahead of the workshops, a group of women performed a song they had written about the sacred nature of women's resistance and struggle and the expansion of women's organisation on the basis of the women's revolution.

Organisational and educational methods discussed




The workshop entitled “The Jineolojî Organisational Model in Europe” examined more than a decade of experience gained through committees, local initiatives, Europe-wide organisational networks and academies. title: KON-MED criticizes CDU MP over remarks about Öcalan
content:
The Confederation of Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED) has strongly criticized remarks by Tijen Ataoğlu, a member of the German Bundestag from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), regarding the imprisonment of Leader Apo, and called on the CDU/CSU parliamentary group and the German government to clarify their positions on the matter.




On 15 October, during a Bundestag session on German-Turkish relations, Tijen Ataoğlu said: “Abdullah Öcalan belongs in prison, and that is absolutely right.”




In a statement published on Friday, the Kurdish umbrella organization described the remark as unacceptable. It said the statement ignored the human rights dimension of Öcalan’s imprisonment and the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR). The fact that Ataoğlu herself serves on the Legal Affairs and Human Rights Committee of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe made the remark particularly serious, it added.




“We expect a lawyer in this position to take European human rights rulings seriously, rather than categorically justifying a person’s imprisonment,” the confederation stated.

title: IHD and ÖHD: Human rights violations are occurring in prisons in Adana
content:
The Adana branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) and the Adana representative office of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) released a report on human rights violations in prisons covering the period from July to September 2026. The report drew attention to solitary confinement, access to healthcare, and other human rights violations at Adana Suluca High-Security Closed Prison and Kürkçüler F-Type Closed Prison.




Serhat Ökmen, a member of the ÖHD, stated that the “pit-type” architecture and penal regime at Suluca Prison cause severe psychological pressure.




Ökmen explained that prisoners spend 23 hours a day in single-person cells and are allowed only one hour outdoors in the exercise yard. Drawing attention to the conditions of isolation in the prison, he said that a prisoner named Nurettin had recently died by suicide.




One of the key issues highlighted in the report was the alleged practice of “intraoral searches” during hospital transfers. Ökmen said that prisoners who refuse to submit to this practice are not transferred to hospitals and are therefore being denied their right to medical treatment.

title: Oruç: Prevention is key to combating drug use
content:
Concerns are growing over drug use, gang activity and social degeneration in Kurdish cities. Human rights organisations have drawn particular attention to the targeting of children and young people, saying that their alienation from social life has serious consequences.




Concerns over drug use, gang activity and social degeneration are continuing to grow in Kurdish cities, with particular attention focused on the targeting of children and young people. Human rights organisations, youth groups and institutions working in the field regard the spread of drugs as part of “special warfare policies”, stressing that the alienation of young people from social life has serious consequences. The increasingly young age of drug users and the expansion of drug networks into neighbourhoods and areas surrounding schools reveal the extent of the threat to young people's futures.




Psychologist Recep Oruç, an activist with the Şiyar Be Anti-Drug Platform, spoke to ANF about the rise in drug use and its negative impact on society.




‘Substance use cannot be attributed to a single cause’




Oruç pointed out that drug use had long been an issue in the cities but had reached a much more serious level over the past five or six years. Oruç said: “We need to look at this issue as a whole. We call on all humanity, particularly the people of Rojava, their families and comrades, to uphold the values created by our fighters for a dignified life and freedom, and to participate in building a democratic and free society as a fulfilment of their commitment to the martyrs' memory.”

This struggle, which we have carried out under women's leadership, has brought about social change and revolutions. The Rojava Women's Revolution emerged as the culmination and highest expression of the accumulated experience and legacy of our 53-year struggle and the entire history of women's struggle. In the fight against ISIS mercenaries, freedom fighters led by Kurdish women rewrote history in favour of the peoples in golden letters, proving that an alternative way of life is possible and becoming a source of hope for the world.”

title: Koma Amara releases ‘Derwêşo’ videoclip in memory of Ali Haydar Kaytan
content:
The music group Koma Amara, composed of women guerrillas, filmed the videoclip of the song “Derwêşo,” dedicated to the memory of martyred Ali Haydar Kaytan, one of the pioneers of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement.




The video, produced by Tarık Demir of Art Media Produktion, was published on Med Huner’s YouTube channel.













The song, performed by Xwezan Harun, was written and composed by Ferîde Rapo, with arrangements by Seyîd Riza Silbûs. The “Derwêşo” video combines footage of Xwezan Harun with photographs of Ali Haydar Kaytan.




Koma Amara's third videoclip




This year, Koma Amara released an album titled Hevala Min, consisting of eight songs. The album features the songs “Derwêşo,” “Sara û Bişeng,” “Vengê Avzem,” “Hevala Min,” “Çar Heval,” “Roniyê Me,” “Roj û Zarok,” and “Kezî.”




The group had previously released music videos for “Hevala Min” and “Roniyê Me.” “Derwêşo” is the third video produced as part of the album.




Making art under difficult conditions




Tarık Demir, who designed Koma Amara’s album cover and handled its promotion, distribution, and licensing, also edited the “Derwêşo” music video.

title: Jineolojî Academy: Jineolojî should be at the heart of social organization
content:
In a message sent to the European Jineolojî Conference, the Jineolojî Academy Board reflected on 11 years of accumulated experience in Jineolojî activities and highlighted the tasks and responsibilities of the new period.




Stating that Jineolojî is rooted in the historical experience of struggle of the Kurdish Women’s Freedom Movement, the board emphasized that its activities should be developed on the basis of building a democratic society and advancing women’s freedom.




Stating that Jineolojî should not be confined to a single committee, the board emphasized that all institutions within the women’s movement should incorporate this perspective into their activities.




“Every individual, institution, organization, and structure working towards social transformation and revolution can achieve their political objectives only through a sound sociological approach,” the message stated.

title: Women discuss Jineolojî experiences and the needs of the new period
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference, held in Haelen, the Netherlands, under the slogan “Bi Jineolojî ber bi avakirina jiyana komunal û azad” (With Jineolojî towards building a communal and free life), continued with its first session, titled “Jineolojî: The Science of Building Women’s Identity on the Basis of Freedom.” The session addressed the experiences, achievements, shortcomings, and perspectives for the new period of Jineolojî activities carried out across Europe.




Jineolojî experience in Europe evaluated




The session began with an extensive visual presentation featuring testimonies from women, photographs, short videos, and audio recordings documenting conferences, camps, educational programs, research initiatives, and committee activities organized or attended by European Jineolojî committees over the years.




The presentation, which traced the development of Jineolojî activities in Europe over the past 15 years, highlighted the considerable knowledge and experience accumulated through conferences, educational programs, research, and camps. It emphasized the need to transform these activities into lasting organizational structures, strengthen ties with local women, and make the knowledge produced accessible throughout society.




The visual presentation examined the development of Jineolojî activities in Europe, their achievements, and the challenges encountered.

title: Bayındır: It is time to open the door wide to freedom, peace, and equality
content:

Speaking during a meeting with representatives of civil society organizations on Friday, Bayındır recalled previous peace processes that had failed to produce results and highlighted the importance of the current Peace and Democratic Society Process.




Stating that the cessation of conflict for the past two years was significant, Bayındır emphasized that resolving the Kurdish question was not simply a matter of laying down arms. He said the Kurdish people’s demands for constitutional recognition and status must also be addressed.




Bayındır described the commission established in parliament as part of the process and efforts to draft a framework law as important but insufficient. He called for the release of political prisoners and legal arrangements that would enable guerrilla fighters and members of the Kurdish diaspora living in Europe to return.




Emphasizing that the process could not advance through statements of goodwill alone, Bayındır said, “The rights and demands of the Kurdish people must be recognized. It is time to open the door wide to freedom, peace, and equality in these lands.”

title: Karabulut: Existing trade unions cannot even protect their own members
content:
Low wages, precarious employment conditions, and increasing obstacles to trade union organizing shape the working lives of millions of people in Turkey. According to the Ministry of Labor and Social Security, only 2.5 million of approximately 17.6 million registered workers are unionized. This means that around 86 percent of officially registered employees are not members of a trade union.




Özgür Karabulut, chair of the Revolutionary Construction and Road Workers’ Union (Dev-Yapı-İş), which is affiliated with the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey (DİSK), sees this as the result of policies that favor employers and systematically hinder workers’ ability to collectively assert their rights. Speaking to ANF, he also criticized traditional trade union structures, arguing that many are no longer capable of representing the interests of their own members.







‘Workers are at the mercy of employers’




Karabulut described working conditions in Turkey as increasingly precarious. He said millions of people were affected by unemployment, low wages, and a lack of social security. The fragmentation of employment into different working arrangements and contractual relationships further complicates efforts to organize collectively, he noted.

title: TUHAY-DER in Mardin calls for the release of political prisoners in Turkey
content:
The Association for Solidarity and Cooperation with Families of Prisoners and Convicts (TUHAY-DER) staged a sit-in outside the courthouse in Mardin, calling for the release of political prisoners and concrete steps in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Under the slogan “Freedom for Prisoners, Hope for Peace,” relatives of political prisoners, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and numerous other people gathered for the protest. A banner read: “No Extensions of Imprisonment – Freedom for Political Prisoners.”




Ayşe Bozan, co-chair of TUHAY-DER’s Mardin branch, particularly criticized the practice of keeping political prisoners behind bars even after they have served their sentences. She said that repeatedly denying their release prevented them from returning to a life of freedom. Many relatives, especially mothers, have long been waiting for the prison gates to finally open, she added.




Bozan pointed to the contradiction between the stated efforts to achieve a democratic and peaceful solution to the Kurdish question and the continued repression within the prison system. “While talks focus on strengthening democratic politics and establishing lasting social peace, practices that prevent equal participation in political and social life remain in place,” she noted.

20 Years of EUTCC Conferences – 20 Demands for Peace and Democracy

title: Hasakah tensions: Are Kurds and Arabs being drawn into conflict?
content:
Rising tensions in Hasakah (Hesekê) in the first days of October 2026 have once again raised concerns about the future of Rojava. Clashes between security forces and protesters were reported in the city on 9 October, with several Kurdish youths reportedly injured. Around the same time, pro-government Arab demonstrators held protests against the Kurdish administration, while counter-protests followed attacks on Kurdish symbols.




The Governor of Hasakah blamed the incidents on groups opposed to the integration agreement. However, this statement does not mean that all those involved in the incidents, or their motives, have been conclusively identified.




To view these developments simply as a dispute that has arisen naturally between Arabs and Kurds would be to overlook their political dimensions.




Hasakah is a strategic city where Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs and other communities live together, and where the future of security and administrative structures is being debated. A large-scale conflict here might not remain confined to a single neighbourhood or city. It could directly affect Rojava's political future, relations between its peoples and the integration process with the Damascus administration.

content:

According to the report, over the past two days, IRGC forces have deployed heavy military equipment and drones around the village of Daleh Marz and subjected parts of the Shaho Mountains in the Dasht-e Qalb area to artillery shelling and aerial bombardment.




Reports also say that the IRGC has prohibited access to this area on the slopes of the Shaho Mountains in recent days. In addition to extensive artillery shelling, IRGC forces have targeted parts of the area with suicide drones.




These military exercises and artillery attacks are taking place despite the fact that the Shaho and Kosalan Mountains were designated as protected areas under the management of Iran’s Department of Environment in 2009, pursuant to Resolution No. 303 of the Supreme Council for the Environment.

title: Grape harvest tradition continues despite drought in Amed
content:
As the weather turns colder, villagers have begun the grape harvest. Grapes are being gathered for winter preparations in vineyards where yields have declined year after year due to the climate crisis and worsening drought across the region. Traditional preparations, particularly in Mardin (Mêrdîn) and Diyarbakır (Amed), continue for days, with women carrying out most of the work.




Residents of Hazro (Hezro) said they were producing less grape molasses than in previous years because of declining yields, adding that recent rainfall had also damaged the grapes.







 







Women taking part in the grape harvest in Dercal village, in the Hazro district of Diyarbakır, spend days preparing food for winter. They gather the grapes, crush them to extract the juice and then boil it. They use the grape juice to make molasses, pestil (dried fruit sheets) and cevizli sucuk (walnuts coated in thickened grape juice). The women leave the products they have prepared through hours of labour to dry in the sun. Villagers rely on these foods throughout the winter.




Remziye Ödüngit has been going to the vineyards with her children every September or October for nearly 30 years to harvest grapes. She spends around a week working during the harvest. Although everyone contributes, Ödüngit said women take on greater responsibilities. She expressed her deep love for her village and land, sayin

title: Aksu: Ecology is better understood, but shallow approaches persist
content:
Ecological destruction and the plundering of nature are increasing day by day in Turkey and Kurdistan. As the environmental impact of projects carried out under the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government's “mega projects” is debated, the loss of forested areas continues.




Cemil Aksu of Polen Ecology spoke to ANF about the ecological destruction taking place in Turkey and Kurdistan, the causes of the plundering of nature and the struggle against it.




Aksu pointed out that 68 percent of forest destruction in Turkey has occurred under AKP rule and said: “The export-led growth strategy pursued by the AKP is turning Turkey into the West's Africa. Turkey's ecological problems began to escalate dramatically under AKP rule. The AKP started with ‘urban transformation’, ‘dual carriageways’, ‘megacities’ and ‘mega projects’, turning the entire country into a construction site. To supply the energy, cement and other raw materials needed for this construction site, it also turned rural areas, valleys and rivers across the country into sites for energy production, mining and other activities.

title: No news of artist Jîna Ehmedî, arrested in Iran, for 10 days
content:
There has been no news for 10 days of artist Jîna Ehmedî, also known as Jîlemo, who was detained by Iranian regime forces in the city of Merîwan in Eastern Kurdistan.




According to Kolber News, Jîna Ehmedî, who is from the village of Nigil in the Merîwan area, was detained by Iranian regime forces at her home in Merîwan. She was subsequently taken to Sine Central Prison. Despite 10 days having passed since her detention, no information has been obtained about her health or whereabouts.




It has been reported that Ehmedî is being held in the women's ward of the prison and has been denied the right to meet with her lawyer, communicate by telephone, or meet with her family in person.




She provided art education to children




Jîna Ehmedî is known as the founder of Jîlemo Music House, which operates in Merîwan.




No explanation has been given for the reasons behind Ehmedî's detention. She founded the institution, which provides children with education in music, singing, painting, and cinema.

title: Resistance against geothermal project in Varto: Court schedules site inspection for November
content:
Resistance against a planned geothermal power plant in the village of Xwarik in the Varto district of Muş province continues. For 165 days, local residents have maintained a protest vigil against the project proposed by the US-based company IGNIS H2 Energy. As the protests continue, the Administrative Court in Bingöl has set a new date for a court-ordered expert inspection of the project site.




Local residents filed a lawsuit against the power plant project on April 9, requesting a suspension of its implementation. On July 21, the court ordered an on-site inspection and the preparation of an expert report. After objections were raised to the inspection initially scheduled for October 8 over the need for a suitably qualified geophysicist, the inspection was postponed to November 2. The project site in the neighboring district of Karlıova is also scheduled to be examined on the same day.




DBP joins protest vigil




The protest vigil, initiated by the Youth Council of the Varto Ecology Platform, is being supported by different groups on a rotating basis. On the 164th day of protests, the local branch of the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) took over the vigil. A banner displayed by the protesters reads: “The people of Varto do not want a geothermal power plant. Hands off our water and our land.”

title: Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî sentenced to more than five years in prison
content:
Kurdish politician and former co-chair of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî (Lahur Sheikh Jangi Talabani), has been sentenced to five years and three months in prison by a court in Sulaymaniyah. His lawyer confirmed the verdict to the news outlet The New Region on Thursday. Talabanî’s brother Polad was also sentenced to three years and six months in prison. The court handed down a two-year prison sentence to their close associate Rebwar Hamid Haci Gali.




Power struggle within the PUK




The case stems from a long-running power struggle within the PUK, one of the two dominant governing parties in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI). Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî led the party alongside Bafel Talabanî until he was removed from power in 2021. The two are cousins, and Bafel Talabanî remains the leader of the PUK. Another cousin, Qubad Talabanî, serves as deputy prime minister of the Kurdistan Region.




Following his removal from the party leadership, Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî founded the opposition People’s Front (Bereyî Gel). In August 2025, PUK-affiliated security forces deployed tanks and drones to arrest the politician at his residence in the Lalezar Hotel in Sulaymaniyah. title: Compulsory expropriation approved for oil extraction in Amed
content:
Two plots of land in the Kocaköy district of Amed (Diyarbakır) are to be expropriated for oil extraction. The land will be used by the state-owned Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) for the Çobantepe-5 drilling site and its associated infrastructure. The decision by the General Directorate of Mining and Petroleum Affairs (MAPEG) under Turkey’s Ministry of Energy was published in the Official Gazette.




The expropriation affects two plots of land covering a total area of 23,333.56 square meters. The plot designated as parcel 143/1 covers 12,926.76 square meters, while the second, designated as parcel 152/2, covers another 10,406.80 square meters.




Previous attempts to acquire the land through mutual agreement had failed because, according to the authorities, the landowners had demanded compensation exceeding market value. Court orders authorizing early possession of both plots had already been issued by the Diyarbakır Court of First Instance.




MAPEG justified the expropriation on the grounds of public interest in oil extraction, citing Article 10, Paragraph 2 of Turkish Petroleum Law No. 6491.

author: Unknown
title: Second death sentence for Warisha Moradi
content:
Warisha Moradi, a Kurdish political prisoner and women’s rights activist, has been sentenced to death for a second time by Branch 15 of Tehran’s Revolutionary Court. This time, the charge is of “membership in a rebel group”.




Her lawyers say the court issued the new sentence without completing the investigations requested by the Supreme Court, and simply changed the charge. The Supreme Court had overturned her first death sentence because of incomplete investigations and procedural violations. Her lawyers say there is insufficient evidence to support the charge and will appeal within the 20-day deadline.




Moradi has been in detention since the summer of 2023.

title: Talabani receives Bakırhan, reaffirms PUK’s support for the peace process in Turkey
content:
Bafel Jalal Talabani, President of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), received Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the DEM Party, in Dabashan.







The meeting on Wednesday was attended by Shanaz Ibrahim Ahmed and Dr Yousif Goran, members of the PUK Political Bureau, and Salar Lala Sarhad, Head of the Kurdistani Relations Board. Discussions focused on continuing joint coordination and cooperation and strengthening bilateral relations in pursuit of shared interests and greater regional stability.







The two sides also exchanged views on the peace process in Turkey. Bafel Talabani reaffirmed the PUK’s support for this historic initiative, stating: “We will continue to follow the same policy pursued by President Mam Jalal until this vital and decisive process succeeds. We believe that peace and coexistence enable us to serve our people, whereas war and division bring nothing but destruction. I therefore hope that everyone will turn a new page and work towards lasting peace.”







For his part, Bakırhan thanked Talabani and the PUK for their efforts to advance the peace process, saying: “We highly value your role and appreciate your steps in support of stability and peaceful coexistence in the region.”







Photos: PUKMEDIA

title: Savary-Borioli: If Turkey wants peace, it must release Öcalan
content:
Swiss politician and emergency physician Dr. Beppe Savary-Borioli believes that a lasting resolution to the Kurdish question is hardly conceivable without Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom and the fundamental democratization of Turkey. Speaking to ANF, the member of the Ticino cantonal parliament expressed serious doubts about the Turkish government’s willingness to secure the current peace process through binding political and legal guarantees. At the same time, he sees Öcalan’s concept of democratic confederalism as offering a perspective that extends beyond the Kurdish question.




Since Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society, the Kurdish freedom movement has taken far-reaching steps toward ending the armed struggle against Turkey. According to Savary-Borioli, however, the future of this process depends crucially on whether Ankara is prepared to establish the political conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement on equal terms.

title: Imprisoned journalist Ahmed Polad’s father: Don’t leave him alone
content:
Journalist Ahmed Polad, who was abducted and detained by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) on 18 January 2026 while covering events in Syria, was handed over to Turkey on 9 September 2026 after spending eight months in HTS prisons. Polad was subsequently arrested in Turkey. His father, Adil Aslan, appealed to the public to draw attention to his son's situation.




Ahmed Polad and Eva Maria Michelmann, who had been working as journalists in Rojava for many years, were abducted on 18 January 2026 during HTS attacks on Raqqa. Following a prisoner exchange on 11 April 2026, testimonies from people held in HTS prisons revealed that both journalists were in detention.




Once their whereabouts became known, campaigns demanding their release were organised in Turkey, Kurdistan and around the world. Following public pressure, HTS handed German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann over to Germany on 18 June 2026.




Eight months of torture in HTS prisons and a padded cell at MIT




Polad's whereabouts were finally confirmed on 9 September 2026. He was handed over to Turkey by HTS and subsequently remanded in custody by a court. In a report documenting his eight months in detention, Polad's lawyers stated that the journalist had been subjected to months of torture by HTS and had contracted scabies because of the unsanitary conditions and inadequate nutrition in prison.

title: Cahit Berkay: Justice will strengthen trust in the peace process
content:
Artists continue to express their support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process through ANF. Musician Cahit Berkay welcomed the silencing of weapons and said swift, concrete steps were needed to advance the process. He stressed that justice was fundamental to peace and drew attention to the importance of freedom to use one's mother tongue.




‘The guns have fallen silent, now further steps must follow’




Musician Cahit Berkay told ANF: “The most important thing was for the guns to fall silent. This was a very welcome decision. Now further steps must follow. The way has been opened for that. It seems this process will be pursued more seriously than previous ones. I hope it achieves its goal.”




Berkay, who described love as his philosophy of life, continued: “My approach to these issues, my philosophy of life, is that love lies at the heart of everything. Peace is something that can be achieved by people who are capable of genuinely and properly feeling, building and experiencing love. Love begins with a person's respect and love for themselves. It then extends to their loved ones, friends, country, the world and the universe. Love also keeps our conscience alive.

content:

Undoubtedly, you have carried out—and continue to carry out—very valuable work, for which I offer my thanks and respect.

I will not refrain from criticizing this at this point. They had said of me that ‘there is not a single patch of land in Europe where he could set foot.’ This conspiracy and these schemes were carried out in secrecy, hidden from the peoples of Europe. They were orchestrated according to the Gladio mentality. Undoubtedly, you are struggling against this situation. You are working to challenge it.




The European Union, which adopted this approach at the time, must today act in accordance with its own laws. It is of great importance that it take a constructive approach both to the democratization of Turkey and to the resolution of the Kurdish question. title: PYD condemns the attack on party office in Hesekê
content:
The Democratic Union Party (PYD) condemned the vandalism of its office in the Xiwêran neighborhood of Hesekê and called for a comprehensive investigation into the attacks. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the party’s leadership described the attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women as a threat to social peace, freedom of political activity, and coexistence among the different communities in northeastern Syria.




On Tuesday, unidentified individuals forcibly entered the PYD office, broke down doors, and vandalized the premises. Kurdish symbols, particularly memorial portraits of prominent women figures of the revolution, were targeted and stolen. Images of fallen women were subsequently desecrated in public, and footage of these acts was circulated on social media. According to the authorities, a suspect has since been arrested.




Connection with attack in Til Temir




The PYD recalled that the Center of the Council of Families of Martyrs in Til Temir had also been attacked just a few days earlier. The party views these incidents as part of a deliberate campaign targeting social coexistence. “The attacks in Til Temir and now in Hesekê, as well as the destruction of our office, indicate a systematic plan aimed at undermining coexistence,” the General Council stated.

title: Devrim Demir: Our relations with Rojava will continue
content:
The visits by a delegation of women traveling from North Kurdistan (Bakûrê Kurdistan) to Rojava are continuing.

After being welcomed at the PYD headquarters, the delegation proceeded to the city municipality. This morning, the delegation first visited the Kongra Star headquarters, followed by visits to the university in Kobanê, the Kobanê Museum, the families of martyrs, the Martyrs’ Cemetery, and Miştenûr Hill.

Rojava needs support

title: Provocations in Hesekê and the importance of self-defence
content:
Hesekê (al-Hasakah) is one of Syria's most diverse cities, home to Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs/Assyrians, Armenians and other communities living side by side. Kurds are concentrated mainly in the Mufti and Salihiyê neighbourhoods, while Arabs predominantly live in Xiwêran, Neşva and Tel Hacer. Different communities live together in Aziziyê and parts of the city centre.




The question of how the city is governed is directly linked to how this multi-ethnic population is represented. The Autonomous Administration model, established in Rojava and regarded as an example for the world, is based on shared governance in which different sections of society have a say. The current Syrian Interim Government in Damascus, however, advocates a return to the mentality of the Ba'ath regime. Although the 29 January Agreement initiated an integration process between Damascus and the Autonomous Administration, the current government continues to refuse to recognise the political will, identity and cultural rights of the Kurds. The murders, attacks on symbols, attempts to occupy Kurdish neighbourhoods and armed incidents witnessed in Hesekê recently have reflected this mentality in the city.

title: Kurdish Conference at the European Parliament: The current opening creates an opportunity
content:
The second day of the Kurdish Conference held at the European Parliament began with opening speeches. Kariane Westrheim of the University of Bergen in Norway, Chair of the EU Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC), which organized the 20th conference, delivered the first speech.




EUTCC 20 years: A voice for Kurdish rights, peace and democracy




Speaking via live video link during the first session, moderated by EUTCC Board Member Dersim Dağdeviren, Kariane Westrheim thanked everyone who had contributed to the conference, saying: “When EUTCC was founded in 2004, Turkey was at an important crossroads. Discussions regarding Turkey's European Union membership had begun, yet the resolution of the Kurdish issue—a central matter of democracy—had not been addressed. We acted with the awareness that this political initiative, detached from reality, would neither democratize Turkey nor resolve the Kurdish issue.”




After outlining the political changes and forms of participation since the conference’s inception, Kariane Westrheim also addressed the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey.

content:

In a statement on Thursday, the organization described the decision as a continuation of state repression against women fighting for freedom and self-determination. It also demanded the immediate annulment of all death sentences and the release of political prisoners sentenced to death.




“The renewed death sentence against Varisheh Moradi reflects the regime’s fear of women’s political will and the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ [Woman, Life, Freedom] movement,” KJAR stated, stressing that this determination would not bow to oppression, repression, or inhumane sentences such as the death penalty.




Resistance against the Iranian judiciary

content:
