title: The opportunity for democratization must not be missed
content:
The leadership of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, which Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan has described as the “Communalist Comradeship Movement,” issued a new and highly significant statement on 8 October regarding the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Announcing that it had withdrawn its guerrilla forces from within Turkey’s borders and evacuated four tunnels in Metîna, the movement’s leadership stated that “there are now no guerrilla forces left that pose a threat to Turkey.”




Undoubtedly, the decision to dissolve the PKK and end its strategy of armed struggle, the act of 30 guerrillas burning their weapons on 11 July 2025, and the steps taken throughout 2025 to withdraw forces that faced a risk of clashes inside Turkey and along the border are all historically significant for advancing the Peace and Democratic Society Process. The steps taken in late September and early October 2026 are equally important. All of these developments demonstrate how seriously the Kurdish side is approaching the process and how courageously it is taking the practical steps that the process requires.

title: Group from Zurich takes over the Freedom for Öcalan Vigil in Strasbourg
content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, which was launched on 25 June 2012, in Strasbourg, has entered its 746thweek.




The vigil, which continues in Strasbourg, where institutions such as the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights are located, was taken over by Barış Çetin, Cihat Kalkan and Cesur Akar from Zurich.




Speaking on behalf of the demonstrators, Barış Çetin emphasized that they were protesting the conditions of isolation imposed for nearly 28 years on Abdullah Öcalan, who was imprisoned in 1999 as a result of an international conspiracy.




“We will continue until our leader’s physical freedom is secured,” Çetin said, adding, “We also want the international community to recognize the struggle taking place here and the reality of the situation. Our comrades have demonstrated their determination for 746 consecutive weeks. Our Leader’s physical freedom is of great importance to us.”




Calling on the international community to fulfill its duties and responsibilities, Çetin stated that stability and peace in the Middle East would only be possible through the freedom of Öcalan.

content:

It holds the Islamist transitional government in Damascus responsible for ensuring security in the city and preventing further attacks.




The statement follows an attack on an office of the Democratic Union Party (PYD) in the Xiwêran neighborhood on Tuesday. An individual entered the premises, damaged portraits of fallen women, and stole Kurdish symbols. Other memorial portraits taken from the office were subsequently desecrated in public. The perpetrator shared footage of these acts on social media. According to the ANHA news agency, the man has since been arrested by the Internal Security Forces.




Attacks target women’s struggle for freedom




Kongra Star placed the incident in the context of increasing attacks on Kurdish values, symbols, and fallen fighters since the mobilization of Arab groups from Deir ez-Zor, Raqqa, Tal Hamis, and al-Shaddadi. title: Court overturns environmental approval for Birsu hydroelectric power plant in Bingöl
content:
The Administrative Court in Bingöl has overturned the environmental approval for the planned Birsu hydroelectric power plant on the Sarim River. The judges unanimously ruled that the positive environmental impact assessment (EIA) decision was unlawful. The ruling was based on an expert report that identified significant scientific and technical deficiencies in the project’s assessment.




The hydroelectric power plant, planned by the company Silvan Elektrik Üretim, is to be built on the Sarim River in the border area between the districts of Lice and Kulp in Amed (Diyarbakır) and the district of Genç in Bingöl. Villagers have been challenging the project through legal channels for several years. They fear serious consequences for the region’s water resources, biodiversity, and agricultural livelihoods.




River flow and dry periods incorrectly assessed




According to the court, the deficiencies in calculating the available water volumes are particularly serious. The river flow data used in the project are not based on measurements taken within the affected river basin. Furthermore, the average river flow was overestimated, contradicting relevant scientific findings.

title: Turkish army blocks road connecting two villages in Til Temir
content:
Turkish occupation forces have blocked the only road connecting the villages of al-Manakh and al-Kanihir, north of Til Temir in northeastern Syria. Turkish soldiers stationed in al-Manakh erected earthen barriers across the road, cutting off the direct connection between the two villages.




According to the ANHA news agency, citing local sources, the Turkish military is also preventing residents from accessing their homes and agricultural land in Turkish-occupied areas.

title: Diyarbakır City Hospital workers demand their rights
content:
Construction workers at the Diyarbakır (Amed) City Hospital construction site, where work began in November 2021, have been subjected to systematic pressure for years. The workers previously staged two protests over unpaid wages and difficult working conditions. Most recently, they launched another protest against dismissals linked to their union membership. The protest, organised by 75 members of the Construction and Road Workers' Union (Yapı Yol-Sen) demanding improved working conditions and the recognition of their employment rights, has continued for 14 days.







 







The workers have continued their protest with traditional halay dances, demanding an end to unfair wage deductions, the underpayment of Social Security Institution (SGK) contributions based on wages lower than their actual earnings, unpaid overtime and Sunday work, and problems concerning travel allowances and workplace safety. They said they faced pressure, threats and the risk of dismissal for exercising their trade union rights and vowed to continue their struggle until their demands were met.




‘We faced workplace bullying because of our union membership’




Yapı Yol-Sen member Mehmet Yariç said that all workers at the construction site, not only union members, were under pressure and that working conditions were deteriorating by the day.

title: Release of two prisoners postponed again
content:
The release of Zeliha Ustabaş, who is held at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, has been blocked for the fifth time by a decision of the Prison Administration and Observation Board.




Ustabaş’s release, which has been postponed four times since 18 July 2024, has now been delayed by a further nine months.




It was reported that Ustabaş’s current sentence period is due to end on 24 July 2027, and that 8 July 2027 has been set as the date for a reassessment of her case.




The release of Orhan Yakışır, who is held at Sincan No. 1 High-Security Prison, has also been postponed, for the third time.




Yakışır’s release was previously postponed by three months on the first occasion and eight months on the second. His release has now been delayed by a further 11 months.




It was stated that the board’s next review of Yakışır’s case will take place on 7 September 2027.

title: Gülsüm Elvan: Peace requires justice and women's struggle
content:
Eighty women from the women's movement, politics, academia, culture and the arts came together on 21 September under the appeal “Side by Side, Talking About the Future”, declaring that resolving the Kurdish question through democratic politics and negotiations would mark a new era for democracy in Turkey.




Gülsüm Elvan, the mother of Berkin Elvan, who was struck by a police-fired tear gas canister during the Gezi Resistance and died at the age of 15 after spending nine months in a coma, spoke to ANF about why she signed the appeal and what peace means for women.




‘Let no more mothers weep, let no more children be killed’




Gülsüm Elvan explained her reasons for signing the appeal, stressing her pursuit of justice and her determination to prevent other families from experiencing the same suffering. Elvan said: “The reason I signed this appeal is clear. I am a mother whose heart has been broken, whose child was taken from her, who has sought justice but has never been able to find it. At the same time, throughout my struggle for justice, whenever I speak about Berkin, I have always said, ‘Let no more mothers weep, let no more children be killed.’”




‘We will bring peace through struggle, women are rising up’

title: Iranian mountaineer and musician Ali-Sina Mustafavi executed
content:
According to Mizan News Agency, affiliated with Iran’s judiciary, Ali-Sina Mustafavi, a 38-year-old from Kerman, was executed on Wednesday. Human rights organisations had warned a day before the execution that it could be imminent after Mustafavi was placed in solitary confinement. Prison authorities were reportedly in contact with his family and had summoned them for a final visit.




Human Rights for Sports, an organisation that advocates for athletes’ rights, had also included Mustafavi, a mountaineer and musician, on its list of athletes at risk of execution. Human rights organisations said that Mustafavi had been forced to confess.




Mizan News Agency accused Mustafavi of carrying out armed attacks in Kerman in which civilians were injured. The report alleged that the attacks were carried out in support of Iran’s Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi and Israel.




Mizan also claimed that Mustafavi had filmed areas that were struck during the war. However, the agency provided no details about the trial proceedings or the evidence presented in court.




Iranian authorities systematically and arbitrarily use charges such as espionage, crimes against national security, armed rebellion, “enmity against God” and “corruption on earth” to prosecute dissidents and protesters. Human rights organisations say these charges are used to portray opponents as security threats and to justify dea

author: Unknown
title: Xebat Kobanê: A war veteran devoted to music and song
content:
Every war veteran who has sacrificed part of their body to protect their land and people in North and East Syria has a different story. Xebat Kobanê is one of them.




Xebat grew up in a patriotic family. One of his brothers was martyred, while one of his sisters joined the ranks of the revolution.







 







Xebat joined the People's Protection Units (YPG) with great enthusiasm and hope. He stood on the front lines of resistance in many areas against treacherous attacks targeting his land and people.




Xebat knew that martyrdom and injury were possibilities on this honourable path. Alongside his military training, he also developed himself ideologically. Conscious of following in the footsteps of Arîn and Rêvan, he took on all aspects of revolutionary work with great dedication.




Xebat Kobanê was wounded during a period of intense fighting, leaving both his legs paralysed. However, he has never regarded his injury as an obstacle. He follows Abdullah Öcalan's perspectives on war veterans and acts on the principle that “veterans are defenders of the revolution”.




Xebat has been interested in music for many years and plays the saz, a traditional long-necked string instrument, with remarkable skill. He also has a beautiful singing voice.




War veteran Xebat Kobanê takes his saz wherever he goes. He plays and sings songs for his fellow war veterans.

author: Unknown
title: Martyr Welat wanted to be the voice of truth
content:
The early days of the Rojava Revolution saw many people living in Rojava seeking to become the voice of their society and expose the attacks, violations and suffering endured by their people. However, this was no easy task. Journalists who decided to document the realities faced by the people encountered numerous difficulties and dangers. Many lost their lives in pursuit of this mission. Many journalists seeking to document the atrocities committed during the Turkish state's occupation attacks on North and East Syria were targeted, particularly during the attacks on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî in October 2019. One of them was martyr Vedat (Welat) Erdemci, who remained determined to be the voice of his people and bring the truth about the region to public attention until his final moments.




Journalist Zinar Cafer spoke to ANF about the life and work of journalist Vedat Erdemci, who was martyred during the attacks on Serêkaniyê on 11 October 2019.







Cafer said that a few words could never adequately convey the stories of the martyrs of the free press and added: “Writing books about the martyrs of the press or speaking about them in programmes is not enough on its own. At the beginning of the Rojava Revolution, many people in Kurdistan wanted to become the voice of their society because we witnessed numerous violations and attacks. The Rojava region of Kurdistan was experienci

author: Unknown
title: Two Iraqi soldiers killed in mine explosion in Kirkuk
content:
An officer and a soldier from the Iraqi army were killed in a mine explosion in Kirkuk on Wednesday. Two other soldiers were injured. The explosion occurred in Wadi Zixêtûn (Zghaitoun), near Reşad (Rashad), when a military vehicle belonging to the 11th Division triggered a previously planted mine.




Among those killed was Ahat Yasir, the division’s communications officer. The unit had been deployed to the area to investigate suspected positions and activities of remaining militants from the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS).




The previous day, the Iraqi Air Force had carried out airstrikes on ISIS positions in the valley south of Kirkuk. The soldiers involved had subsequently been dispatched on a reconnaissance mission.

author: Unknown
title: YPJ: Attack on the images of our martyrs is an assault on the honour and values of our society
content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) released a statement condemning the attacks against the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.




The YPJ statement on Wednesday said: “Recently, despicable attempts and attacks have targeted images of our martyrs and the sanctity they represent, which are among the most sacred values of our people and our revolution. These attacks, which directly target the dignity of our martyrs, violate the fundamental principles of humanity, moral awareness, and the inviolable red lines of society’s conscience.”




The statement stressed that: “Our martyrs are our identity, our honour, and the most sacred values underpinning our existence. Those who were defeated by the will and resistance of free women are now attacking our martyrs through inhumane methods that go beyond all standards of human morality. These immoral scenes and despicable acts are in no way befitting our people or our homeland. Such attacks constitute a direct assault on the honour and values of our entire society.”




The YPJ General Command called on the Damascus government to assume its responsibility, take immediate action against these inhumane acts, and hold those responsible fully accountable to the fullest extent possible. YPJ vowed that: “We will not remain silent in the face of these attacks, and no violation of the sanctity of our martyrs will go

author: Unknown
title: Families condemn the attack on the images of martyrs: We will continue on the path of our martyrs
content:
Rojin Mohammad, a founding member of the Martyrs’ Families Foundation in Kobanê, expressed her dismay at the attacks targeting images of martyrs in Hesekê, stating, “We will not accept such immoral acts.”




Rojin Mohammad explained that, for several days, certain groups have been systematically spreading chaos in the al-Khuwairan neighbourhood of Hesekê and attacking images of the martyrs.




“This is an attack on all peoples”




Speaking about the attacks, Rojin Mohammad said: “These martyrs sacrificed their lives for the freedom of Syrian soil and to protect all peoples from massacres. Attacking their images is not an attack on their families alone; it is an attack on all our values. This is a clear violation of the law.”




“The aim is to derail the integration process”




Mohammad pointed out that the aim of these attacks is to undermine the integration process in Syria. She continued: “This chaos and recklessness will not allow Syria to achieve integration or reach a positive outcome. On the contrary, these acts are an attempt to obstruct the integration process. The Syrian state must take notice of these attacks, put an end to these acts of sabotage, and hold those responsible accountable.”




“We will continue on their path”




Rojin Mohammad concluded her message by saying: “A democratic and free Syria must be built through the joint efforts of all its component

author: Unknown
title: Aynur Sarıca: Women must play a founding role in the peace process
content:
Aynur Sarıca of the Jineolojî Academy drew attention to the role women must play in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that pressure and attacks against the women's movement in Kurdistan were continuing.




Sarıca said women must not be confined to following the process or being represented on monitoring commissions, stressing that their participation in decision-making mechanisms was crucial to building a democratic society.




Sarıca said women had played an important role in shaping social life throughout history, but that the nation-state mentality and patriarchal structures continued to attack women's labour, identity and lives. She added that women's historical role had been pushed into the background in dominant narratives.







 







Sarıca said women had often been treated as spoils of war or as instruments for ensuring the continuation of a lineage during periods of war and conflict, but had fought throughout history to defend their existence against such attacks.




She said attacks on women's identity, children, labour and social life had continued through different methods as conflicts intensified in Kurdistan. She added that operations and detentions targeting the women's movement were intended to prevent the struggle for women's freedom from taking root throughout society.




Sarıca said: “Women have asserted their struggle for existence in

author: Unknown
title: Peace Mothers join 'Tuesdays Against Executions' campaign
content:
The Kurdistan Peace Mothers issued a statement regarding their participation in the 'Sêşema Na ji bo Darvekirinê' ('Tuesdays Against Executions') campaign.




The statement drew attention to how Iran’s regime, through its unfair courts, sentences political prisoners and civilians to mass executions every day on baseless charges. It said: “With each passing day, the shadow of the executioner regime weighs more heavily on prisoners.”




Emphasizing that life, freedom, and human dignity are fundamental and inalienable rights, the statement stressed that no mother should be forced to live in fear of her child being executed. It continued: “Execution does not merely bring one person’s life to an end; it also condemns a family to suffer forever. An execution leaves a profound impact on a family for the rest of its life. We offer our support to families who have lost their loved ones.




We demand that the fate of the prisoners be clarified as soon as possible. We call on all families, human rights organizations, and defenders of freedom to be the voice of the prisoners until freedom is secured, and the truth comes to light.”

author: Unknown
title: Police raid Halk TV: broadcast suspended, trustee appointed
content:
Police raided Halk TV’s headquarters in Istanbul in the early hours of Wednesday morning. A trustee was appointed, and its television broadcast was halted. While police searches of the building continued, the road where the channel is located was closed to traffic, and employees were denied entry to the building.




Reporting on the latest developments inside the building after police entered Halk TV, channel presenter Deniz Bayramoğlu said: “Halk TV Editor-in-Chief Suat Toktaş held talks with the head of the trustee board about continuing the broadcast, but the talks were inconclusive. The broadcast has been suspended.”




As part of the investigation, arrest warrants were issued for 17 people, and 11 people were reportedly taken into custody.




Halk TV Board Chair Cafer Mahiroğlu also announced the police raid on social media. Mahiroğlu said: “Kılıçdaroğlu, the leader of the annulment faction, and his team may be happy. The police are at Halk TV.”




Press organisations and unions protest the attack on press freedom




The appointment of a trustee to Halk TV and the suspension of its broadcast prompted protests from press organisations and journalists’ unions. DISK Basın-Iş, the Contemporary Journalists’ Association (ÇGD), and the Journalists’ Union of Turkey (TGS) condemned the decision as interference in press and freedom of expression.




DİSK Basın-Iş stated that t

author: Unknown
title: Ecological destruction in the Zilan Valley continues
content:
Construction work on an irrigation canal in the Zilan Valley (Geliyê Zîlan), near the district of Erciş in Van province, is causing increasing damage to the region’s ecosystem. Since September 23, heavy construction machinery has been operating in the canyon as part of the so-called Pay Irrigation Canal Project. Excavation and construction work in the streambed and surrounding areas have altered the natural flow of water. Water levels have dropped significantly, and some sections of the stream have already dried up.




These developments threaten not only to have serious consequences for local wildlife and vegetation but also to exacerbate water supply problems in the region. Environmental activists have initiated legal proceedings against the project and requested a suspension of construction work. A court decision is still pending, while machinery continues operating in the valley.




Trees felled and riverside vegetation destroyed




The areas along the streambanks have been particularly severely affected. Trees have been felled and large sections of natural vegetation cleared within the valley. The grasses, shrubs, and trees growing in the area perform essential functions in maintaining the ecological balance: they stabilize the soil, prevent erosion, regulate water levels, and provide habitats for numerous animal species.




With the destruction of this vegetation, the

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish literature and cultural memory meet at Frankfurt Book Fair
content:
The 78th Frankfurt International Book Fair, which opened on 7 October in Frankfurt, Germany, concluded on Sunday evening, 11 October. The fair brought together publishing houses, writers, cultural institutions, journalists, academics and representatives of the publishing industry from around the world.




A total of 4,131 exhibitors participated in the fair, which hosted more than 3,600 events.




As one of the international meeting points for the book and publishing industry, the fair also provided a platform for discussions on literature, culture, freedom of expression, democracy, human rights and the future of technology.




‘Czechia was the guest of honour’




Czechia was this year's guest of honour at the Frankfurt Book Fair.




Under the theme “Ein Land an der Küste” (A Country on the Coast), Czechia established a 2,300-square-metre exhibition space at the fair. The Guest of Honour Pavilion hosted events covering various literary genres, with the participation of 75 writers.




The pavilion showcased Czech literature and the country's cultural heritage, incorporating artificial intelligence and interactive technologies. Visitors engaged with digital installations, while a live-drawing robot and interactive poetry applications attracted particular attention.




More than 40 publishing houses took part in Czechia's national presentation, showcasing their books and ho

author: Unknown
title: Tosun: The case is not over until the third attacker is punished
content:
One year has passed since journalist, documentary filmmaker and environmental activist Hakan Tosun was beaten to death in the street in Esenyurt.




Tosun died after suffering a brain haemorrhage at the scene when he was assaulted by two people on the night of 10–11 October 2025 while on his way to visit his mother in the Mehmet Akif Ersoy neighbourhood of Esenyurt district.




Abdurrahman Murat and Adnan Şahin, responsible for Hakan Tosun's death, were summoned to the Esenyurt Mevlana Police Station to give statements and were arrested on charges of intentional injury. However, it was notable that Yusuf Özakdağ, a third person who had also participated in the attack, was questioned as a witness by the same police station.




Although a report by the Council of Forensic Medicine confirmed that Hakan Tosun had been severely beaten, the 17th High Criminal Court accepted the indictment for intentional injury prepared by the Büyükçekmece Chief Public Prosecutor's Office. Following months of proceedings, Abdurrahman Murat and Adnan Şahin were sentenced to life imprisonment for intentional killing. However, the verdict brought no sense of relief to the Tosun family.




Hakan Tosun's sister, Öznur Tosun, spoke to ANF and stressed that the case would not be over until Yusuf Özakdağ, who also participated in the fatal attack on her brother and has openly posed with firearms on socia

author: Unknown
title: BaBa Zula: We stand for peace, the government must act
content:
Artists continue to share messages of peace through ANF. Members of the music group BaBa Zula said artists should take a political stance and called for Kurdish and all other languages spoken in the country to be free.




The musicians said: “The Justice and Development Party (AKP) does not inspire confidence. For peace to come, democracy, rights and the rule of law must come first. Thousands of our people from Anatolia and Mesopotamia have lost their lives. Peace is not a concession granted from above or a political favour. It means people being able to live freely, with their fundamental rights, mother tongues and cultures protected under a fair legal system.”




Murat Ertel, Esma Ertel and Levent Akman of the music group BaBa Zula answered ANF's questions.




‘Artists are being prevented from taking political positions’




Members of BaBa Zula said the group seeks to preserve the multicultural and multilingual heritage of Anatolia, Mesopotamia and Istanbul through its music. They said: “We are living under a cultural bombardment. There is a situation being created, particularly in the virtual world. It is as though the world is being shaped not by its seven billion people, but by the leaders of a population of just one billion. They are also trying to shape culture, but we are interested in the culture of the geography we live in. We eat the food of this region, listen t

author: Unknown
title: The people of Shengal must decide their own future
content:
More than 6,000 people were abducted during the attack on Shengal by ISIS mercenaries on 3 August 2014, and around 2,500 remain missing. The Yazidis refer to the attack, in which thousands of people were massacred and abducted, as the 74th Ferman in their history.




Shengal was liberated from ISIS in 2015. In the aftermath of the Ferman (Shengal genocide), the Yazidis established their own administrative and defence mechanisms, forming a People's Council and defence forces such as the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and Shengal Women's Units (YJŞ). The autonomous administration, which has operated in practice in Shengal ever since, continues to exist as an expression of the people's determination to govern and defend themselves.




Turkey-Iraq trade-off in New York




Turkish President Tayyip Erdoğan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi met in New York on 23 September 2026 while attending the United Nations (UN) General Assembly. The joint statement issued after the meeting highlighted two main points: the full restoration of state authority in Shengal and the elimination of forces described in the statement as “prohibited foreign armed elements”, and the gradual transfer of the Turkish army's Bashiqa (Zilkan) base to the Iraqi federal government. The transfer process was made conditional on security measures to be taken by Iraq and a timetable to be agreed upon by both sides.

author: Unknown
title: PACE delegation meets with the DEM Party in Ankara, discusses the peace process
content:
Petra Bayr, President of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), held talks with the DEM Party during her official visit to Turkey on Monday. Accompanied by her delegation, she met with Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları, Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Sezai Temelli, and MP Sevilay Çelenk, who is a member of the Turkish delegation to PACE, at the Turkish Parliament.




The discussions focused on the role of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Reference was made to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) concerning the so-called “right to hope.” DEM Party representatives emphasized that Öcalan must be provided with living and working conditions that would allow him to participate freely in the peace process.




The discussions also addressed the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) rulings concerning imprisoned politicians Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as human rights activist and cultural philanthropist Osman Kavala, which have yet to be implemented. The Council of Europe delegation expressed its concern regarding these issues. Further meetings with political representatives in Turkey are scheduled as part of the official visit.

author: Unknown
title: ‘Women, Justice and Memory Vigil’ against femicides in its second week
content:
The Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) Network for Combating Violence launched a “Women, Justice and Memory Vigil” against femicides and suspicious deaths of women last Tuesday, October 6. The vigil outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse will continue at the same location every Tuesday for 10 weeks.




Participants displayed a banner reading “Women Hold a Vigil for Justice and Memory,” along with photographs of women who had been killed.  Representatives of numerous political parties and civil society organizations attended the vigil in its second week.




Reading the statement on behalf of the Rosa Women’s Association, Ruşen Yakut said that during this week’s vigil, they were bringing together in collective memory the stories of women who were killed in different cities across Turkey between October 2 and 12 and whose information they had been able to obtain.




Emphasizing that the struggle for justice for murdered women is not limited to any particular period, Yakut stated that they would never abandon their demand for truth and justice. “For us, memory means remembering, leaving a trace, and ensuring that these women are not forgotten. The pursuit of justice means carrying the collective responsibility to protect women’s right to life into the present,” she said.




Following the statement, the stories of Füsun Yuluğkural, Gözde Çelik, Emel Bozkuş, Fadime Akbal, Gülşah Oktay, Sakine Y, F

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish women’s movement participates in 39th Plurinational Gathering of Women in Argentina
content:
The 39th Plurinational Gathering of Women and Gender-Diverse People, held in Córdoba, Argentina from October 10 to 12, brought together hundreds of thousands of women from across Latin America. Organized by 300 local organizations, the gathering featured workshops, panel discussions, film screenings, and meetings.







 








A delegation from the Kurdish women’s movement participated in a meeting on internationalism, organized jointly with the Abya Yala feminist network, a panel titled “Revolutionary Practices,” and a screening of the film 

In Search of Alina

. The events addressed the experiences of Kurdish women, the women’s revolution in Rojava, the struggle of women guerrillas in the mountains of Kurdistan, and the importance of international solidarity.




At the meeting on internationalism organized by the Kurdish women’s movement and the Abya Yala feminist network, discussions focused on the international dimension of Kurdish women’s struggle and the importance of the “Women Weaving the Future” network. Participants chanted the slogan, “Plurinational, plurinational; from Abya Yala to Kurdistan!”




During the panel titled “Revolutionary Practices,” the delegation spoke about the women’s revolution in Rojava, the struggle of women guerrillas in Kurdistan, and the role of internationalism. Following questions from participants, the delegation also addressed the P

author: Unknown
title: Conditions that gave rise to the Kurdish question and the conflict remain unchanged
content:
The conflict between the Turkish state and the PKK has been at a standstill for two years. The PKK has dissolved itself and decided to end its armed struggle against Turkey. The PKK disbanded and took significant steps in 2025 and 2026. All these steps were taken to enable free and unrestricted participation in democratic politics and to achieve a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question.




From the statement issued by the Kurdish Movement Leadership on October 8, we learn that the Turkish state has taken no steps apart from allowing meetings on Imralı Island every few months. More precisely, the Movement Leadership has conveyed this reality, which we have also witnessed, in the form of a polite warning. The statement emphasized that there is no longer any justification for the Turkish state’s failure to act following the significant steps taken by the movement.




The Movement Leadership stated that their leader must be freed and that legislation on freedoms, which would pave the way for a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question, must be enacted without delay. They specifically emphasized that if the Turkish state fails to take steps demonstrating such political will, they will interpret this as an intention to continue its previous policies.




The Movement Leadership made it clear that if the Turkish state takes no action and instead continues to demand furthe

author: Unknown
title: A new chapter in the heart of Paris: Kurdistan House of France
content:
The Kurdistan House of France, which aims to bring together the cultural, social, academic, and institutional activities of the Kurdish community in France under one roof, was officially unveiled to the public at a grand ceremony held at Paris City Hall.




The event, held on the evening of Monday, October 12, in the historic hall of Paris City Hall, located in the political and historical heart of the French capital, brought together politicians, institutional representatives, artists, academics, association leaders, and civil society figures from the Kurdish and French communities.




Three speeches were delivered during the evening. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire gave the opening address, followed by Baran Gürbüz, President of the Kurdistan House of France. Former French President François Hollande delivered the final political address of the evening.




Official launch at historic Paris City Hall




The decision to hold the official launch of the Kurdistan House of France (Maison du Kurdistan de France) at Paris City Hall itself was one of the evening’s most significant symbolic and political messages.




Relations between the Paris municipal administration and Kurdish institutions have become increasingly visible in recent months. In June, Grégoire received representatives of the Democratic Kurdish Council in France and the Kurdistan House of France at City Hall. Their

author: Unknown
title: Botan: Disarmament is a precondition for peace, not peace itself - Part Two
content:
Politician Lezgin Botan spoke to ANF about how the process is viewed by the Kurdish public, political and legal expectations, the relationship between disarmament and democratisation, and possible developments in the coming period.




The first part of this interview can be read 

here

. 




Botan said strengthening local governments and ending the practice of appointing trustees were among the important issues in the process. He stressed that strengthening local democracy should be considered not only in relation to the Kurdish question but also in the context of Turkey's overall democratisation.




Botan also said: “Local democracy is an important issue in the democratic resolution of the Kurdish question. The constant supervision of local governments by the central administration, and their being rendered ineffective when deemed necessary, create serious problems for the political will of the people. The practice of appointing trustees, in particular, means that the central administration appoints officials to replace elected representatives. Overriding the will expressed by the people through elections poses a serious problem for democratic representation. Strengthening local governments should not be seen solely as a demand of Kurds. This is an issue concerning Turkey's overall democratisation. The European Charter of Local Self-Government, which Turkey has signed, sho

author: Unknown
title: Whereabouts of 5 Kurdish men arrested in Baneh remain unknown
content:
The fate of Hesen Mistefayî, Şerzad Çawşînî, Şahîn Reşîdzade, Xusrew Kerempûrî, and Muhyedîn Banerîzî, who were arrested by Iranian intelligence forces in Baneh, in Kurdistan Province, remains unknown.




According to information reported by the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), Iranian intelligence forces raided the family home of Muhyedîn Banerîzî, a resident of Baneh, in the early hours of 9 October 2026, and arrested him.




Xusrew Kerempûrî, who also lives in Baneh, was detained on October 7 during a raid on his family’s home.




Hesen Mistefayî, a well-known philanthropist in the city, was arrested by Iranian intelligence forces on October 6 while taking his child to the hospital. It was reported that, following Mistefayî’s arrest, intelligence agents left his child alone on the street.




Şerzad Çawşînî, originally from Sardasht and residing in Baneh, and Şahîn Reşîdzade were also arrested by Iranian intelligence forces on October 3 and September 26, 2026, respectively.




According to the KHRN, all five men were arrested without court warrants. Since their arrests, no information has been made available regarding their whereabouts, health conditions, or legal proceedings.

author: Unknown
title: Kariane Westrheim: A democratic solution to the Kurdish question would also benefit Turkish society
content:
Prof. Kariane Westrheim, President of the European Union Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC), said that one of the most critical issues to be addressed at the 20th Kurdish Conference at the European Parliament this year would be the ongoing process in Turkey, stressing that this opportunity must not be missed.




We spoke with Prof. Kariane Westrheim of the University of Bergen in Norway about the 20th Kurdish Conference, which will take place at the European Parliament on 14–15 October. Westrheim explained the need that led to the establishment of the conference and reflected on developments over the past two decades. She also outlined the main topics of the 20th conference, identifying the Peace and Democratic Society Process underway in Turkey as the most critical issue. “We need to make use of this process. We must not miss this opportunity,” the EUTCC President said.




Drawing attention to Europe’s declining influence on and interest in Turkey, Westrheim emphasised: “Europe has often refrained from using its influence consistently on issues of democracy, human rights and the rule of law. This is regrettable.”




Professor Westrheim, this year you are organizing the 20th Kurdish Conference in Europe. Why and how did you feel the need to initiate and sustain such a conference?

author: Unknown
title: Özkan: ‘Trust in the process rests on Öcalan’s freedom and lasting peace’
content:
Canan Kebenç Özkan, Co-Spokesperson of the Democratic Local Governments Board of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the approach of local governments to the process, communal life, and Abdullah Öcalan’s status and position.




Canan Kebenç Özkan said the call for Peace and Democratic Society issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February had marked a new stage in the conflict, opening a period in which the Kurdish question must be resolved through peaceful means, on a democratic basis and through democratic politics, rather than through conflict.




Özkan said society was undergoing change and transformation, rebuilding itself on a democratic basis, while the state was becoming more responsive to society and democracy. However, she pointed out that the process was encountering obstacles at certain stages.




‘Öcalan’s role is vital’




Canan Kebenç Özkan said Abdullah Öcalan’s role could not be overlooked at this critical stage of the process, stressing that his contribution must be given the recognition it deserves.




Özkan said: “Öcalan’s vital role in this process absolutely cannot be ignored. His role must be properly recognised. At the same time, people across Kurdistan have very high expectations of the process. There is a strong social expectation that lasting peace will be achieved and a de

author: Unknown
title: Demo in London says Öcalan’s freedom is fundamental condition for peace
content:
The international conspiracy launched on 9 October 1998 against Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan was protested with a march held in London on its 28th anniversary.




Kurds from Kurdistan and their supporters gathered in front of Wood Green Library for the demonstration, organized under the leadership of the London Communities Union. Flags bearing photographs of Öcalan were carried, while banners and placards calling for the implementation of the right to hope and the securing of Öcalan’s physical freedom were displayed.







 








Speakers at the gathering emphasized that the international conspiracy launched on October 9, 1998, targeted not only Öcalan but also the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom and their democratic will. The speakers pointed out that, despite the 28 years that have passed, Önder Apo’s freedom has still not been secured. They stated that the Kurdish people have not abandoned their demands for freedom and a democratic solution.




Highlighting the historical significance of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the speakers stressed that, for the process to lead to a lasting solution, Öcalan must be granted the conditions necessary to work freely, communicate, and engage in negotiations.




The demonstration once again called for the implementation of the right to hope and the securing of Öcalan’s physical freedom, emphasizing his ro

author: Unknown
title: Special and psychological warfare propaganda targeting the process
content:
The dialogue and negotiation process surrounding the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which has been progressing over the past two years at what could be described as a painfully slow pace, has reached a critical juncture. The process appears to be experiencing turbulence, while the deepening climate of uncertainty is weakening public confidence.




Devlet Bahçeli's election-related remarks at the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) parliamentary group meeting appear to indicate that a policy is being pursued to extend the process into the election period. As developments unfold in this way, the slow pace or prolongation of the process creates more opportunities for groups seeking to interfere with it. It also provides fertile ground for the complaints of those opposed to the process and the hostile rhetoric of pro-government media.




Alongside attacks on Peoples’ Leader Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement by fascist, nationalist and profiteering groups opposed to the process, the disinformation and aggressive rhetoric spread by pro-government media align with the forces seeking war rather than peace. Their primary objective is to create a sense of resignation and despair among the public and democratic forces.




Throughout world history, major propaganda campaigns have shaken societies, drawing on particular sources and methods.

author: Unknown
title: Dîlan Cûdî Saruhan: Society should stand by artists, and artists should stand by society
content:
ANF spoke with artist Dîlan Cûdî Saruhan, one of the signatories of the “1,001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign announced on 12 September, about the role of art and artists in the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




We met with Dîlan Cûdî Saruhan at her exhibition titled “Îhtîmaleke Asîman / A Sky of Possibility,” which opened on 22 September. She is the daughter of a family that migrated from Eruh to Istanbul in 1993 during the forced evacuation of villages. The artist, who was held at Bakırköy Women’s Closed Prison from 2017 to 2024, describes the works featured in the exhibition as follows: “In my works, I have depicted my own ten-year journey. This period encompasses three stages of my life: one before prison, another during my time in prison, and the final stage, which is the transition to freedom.”




Dîlan Cûdî Saruhan, who says she works across multiple disciplines, focuses on subjects such as memory, space, freedom, human rights, and ecology in her art.




“Artists must keep the process and its memory alive”




After her release from prison, one of the most important concepts she began to question was freedom. We started our conversation with Dîlan Cûdî Saruhan in front of her work titled “Laş / Body.” In this piece, in which she uses a wall as a metaphor, Dîlan Cûdî portrays the resistance of a body that dissolves into the wall while s

author: Unknown
title: MHP Deputy Chairman expects results in the peace process by the end of November
content:
As part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, MHP (Nationalist Movement Party) Deputy Chairman Feti Yıldız expects concrete results by the end of November. Following this, legal procedures are expected to be initiated for prisoners incarcerated for so-called terrorism-related offenses. According to Yıldız, around 2,800 people could benefit from the legal provisions. However, founding members of the PKK are expected to be excluded.




Yıldız spoke to Sabah columnist Yavuz Donat about the next stages of the peace process. AKP Deputy Chairman Hüseyin Yayman also took part in the talk. Both politicians are members of the parliamentary Commission for National Solidarity, Fraternity and Democracy and were among the representatives who met with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on the prison island of İmralı on behalf of parliament.




“No one can say they are not involved”




Yayman described the peace process as a matter that concerns both the state and society and must be advanced with restraint. “Such things are not achieved through talking, but through silence,” he said. At the same time, he pointed to the government’s existing “red lines.” According to Yayman, a public opinion poll conducted in September showed 73.4 percent support for the process. He described the framework law, adopted by the Turkish parliament with 467 votes, as a safeguard for the next stages of the p

author: Unknown
title: Mohamed: Attacks in Heseke an attempt to undermine Kurdish-Arab coexistence and regional stability
content:
Ruksen Mohamed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), spoke about the dangers posed by the recent attacks in the city of Heseke. She considered the targeting of women’s symbolism and the denigration of their struggle and sacrifices to be attempts to undermine stability and incite discord among the components of Syrian society, particularly Kurds and Arabs.




Ruksen Mohamed stressed that women have demonstrated their ability to bring about positive change through their struggle and their political, social, organisational, and military participation. She noted that the experience of women in Rojava has established their fundamental role in building a society characterised by peace and stability and respect for diversity.




She also explained that attacks on women’s values, existence, and will reflect a mindset seeking to weaken society and dismantle the bonds between peoples. She emphasised that these practices are not coincidental, but rather part of a plan carrying messages that threaten social cohesion, security, and stability.




The YPJ spokesperson further stressed that targeting Kurdish women, their sacrifices, and their standing threatens coexistence among the peoples of the region and opens the door to further tensions and division.




Ruksen Mohamed affirmed that recognising women’s existence, identity, and will is an essential condition for any ser

author: Unknown
title: Future Syria Party demands justice seven years after the murder of Hevrîn Xelef
content:
On the seventh anniversary of the murder of Kurdish politician Hevrîn Xelef, the Future Syria Party (Arabic: Hizbul Suri Mustakbel, Kurdish: Partiya Sûriyeya Pêşerojê) called on the international community to hold those responsible for the crime accountable. In a statement marking the anniversary on October 12, the party leadership commemorated its former secretary-general, who was murdered in 2019 by members of an Ankara-backed jihadist militia during the Turkish invasion of Rojava.




Commitment to a democratic and decentralized system




Xelef, who was also known as the “Jasmine of Peace,” was killed together with her driver, Ferhad Ramadan, near Qamişlo. The Future Syria Party paid tribute to her as a symbol of the resistance of Syrian women and as a voice for peace, national unity, and opposition to policies of occupation. “Hevrîn Xelef was not only an outstanding political trailblazer but remains a role model for women’s social struggle in Syria,” the party stated.




The party remarked that Xelef’s murder did not break the political will to establish a pluralistic, democratic, and decentralized system, but instead strengthened it. “We reaffirm our goal of a political system in which the rights of all social and ethnic communities in Syria, as well as their participation in shaping their future, are guaranteed.”




At the same time, the party renewed its condemnation

author: Unknown
title: YRJ commemorates journalists Dilîşan Îbiş and Dilovan Gever
content:
The Association of Women Journalists in Rojava (YRJ) commemorated journalists Dilîşan Îbiş and Dilovan Gever on the anniversary of their deaths. Both journalists were killed while reporting on the war in North and East Syria. In a statement on Monday, the organization paid tribute to their efforts to document war crimes, highlight the suffering of civilians, and convey the realities of society.




Dilîşan Îbiş documented the suffering of civilians




Dilîşan Îbiş was among the media professionals who reported directly from the scenes of events following the beginning of the Rojava Revolution on July 19, 2012. Working under dangerous conditions for the ANHA news agency, she documented developments on the ground and brought the plight of civilians to international attention.




On October 12, 2017, she was killed in an attack by the Islamic State (ISIS) terrorist group while reporting on civilians fleeing the area during the final anti-ISIS offensive in Deir ez-Zor. Other members of the independent press were also killed alongside her.




“Dilîşan Îbiş was among the women journalists who consciously chose to be at the heart of events. Her death exemplified the dangers faced by journalists documenting the truth under wartime conditions,” YRJ stated.




Dilovan Gever reported on the resistance against the Turkish offensive




The association stated that Dilovan Gever (Dilan Ö

title: Syriac Federation condemns demolition measures in İdil
content:
The International Syriac Federation of Azech has strongly condemned the demolition measures targeting Syriac residents in the İdil district of Şırnak province.




In a written statement, the federation accused Mayor Türkan Kayır and municipal council member Ekrem Şimşek of using the municipal administration as a tool for personal vendettas. The measures reportedly targeted families who had returned to their homeland after decades of displacement.




On October 6, the municipal administration ordered the demolition of a residential and commercial building belonging to Alyet Karagöl. In addition, four other residential buildings and the newly constructed guesthouse of the Syriac Orthodox Church of St. Mary were sealed off. The municipality justified the measures by citing violations of building regulations.










https://twitter.com/gazetesabro/status/2107848754317447376










“We expected impartial municipal governance”




The federation recalled that Türkan Kayır was elected mayor on the DEM Party ticket in the 2024 local elections. “The Syriacs, Kurds, and other residents of İdil expected the elected mayor to govern impartially,” the statement said. Instead, Kayır allegedly began targeting members of the Syriac community who had criticized her policies. According to the federation, she was significantly influenced by municipal council member Ekrem Şimşek, whom the f

author: Unknown
title: Talabani says PUK ready to protect Kurdistan amid regional tensions
content:
Bafel Jalal Talabani, President of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), has warned that the region is facing a precarious situation, stressing the need for greater preparedness, political agreements and cooperation to address mounting security and economic challenges.




Speaking during a panel discussion at the Middle East Research Institute (MERI) Forum 2026 in Erbil on Monday, Talabani said the global economic downturn, alongside the security and economic risks facing Iraq and the Kurdistan Region, made it essential for political forces to work towards practical solutions.




“We must all support the peace process,” he said, adding that the PUK was strengthening its historic relationships across different sectors while maintaining strong international ties and engaging with a broad range of political parties.




During the session, titled “

Building a Stronger Kurdistan: Unity, Security, and Regional Partnerships

”, Talabani discussed developments in the Kurdistan Region, Iraq and the wider region, as well as international affairs and possible ways to address current challenges.




Addressing the PUK’s international relations, Talabani said he was proud of the party’s ties with the United States, Iran, Russia, the United Kingdom and other countries.




“However, the PUK has never been, nor will it ever be, subservient to anyone,” he said. “Anyone who claims that th

author: Unknown
title: MSD remembers Hevrîn Xelef, calls for the perpetrators to be held accountable
content:
The Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) released a statement marking the seventh anniversary of the assassination of Kurdish politician Hevrîn Xelef (Hevrin Khalaf), Secretary General of the Future Syria Party and member of the Syrian Democratic Council’s Presidential Council. Xelef was extrajudicially executed on October 12, 2019, by Turkish-backed Syrian armed groups during the military offensive targeting Serekaniye (Ras al-Ayn) and Gire Spi (Tal Abyad).




MSD said that Xelef’s targeted killing remains a stark reminder of the systematic abuses committed against civilian political leaders during that campaign, stating: “Hevrîn Xelef championed political engagement as the key to uniting Syria’s diverse ethnic and religious communities and advocated for women’s full participation in public life. Her work was driven by a commitment to inclusive dialogue, mutual respect, and minority rights. She dedicated her career to building a democratic, pluralistic Syria where all citizens have a voice in shaping their nation’s future.”




The Syrian Democratic Council emphasized that Xelef’s political legacy is more relevant today than ever: “Achieving long-term stability requires establishing a democratic, decentralized state grounded in equal citizenship, political pluralism, protected civil rights, and women’s leadership. A stable Syria cannot be built on power monopolies or political exc

author: Unknown
title: Father of journalist Ahmet Polad: My son is not receiving medical treatment in prison
content:
Kurdish journalist Ahmet Polad (real name Mehmet Nizam Aslan) is not receiving adequate medical care at Marmara Prison in Silivri, in Istanbul, despite serious health problems. His father, Adil Aslan, who visited him on October 6, told Mezopotamya Agency (MA) about his son’s untreated injuries and the consequences of eight months in captivity under the Islamist group HTS in Syria. The journalist was handed over to Turkey’s National Intelligence Organization (MİT) in early September and subsequently imprisoned in Istanbul’s Metris Prison.




Months of uncertainty about his fate




Adil Aslan described the desperate search for his son, who had been abducted while working as a journalist in Syria. For a long time, the family did not know whether he was still alive. The first clues came from former prisoners. One eyewitness reported the abduction of Polad and his German colleague Eva Maria Michelmann. On April 11, a released prisoner confirmed having seen the journalist in detention. At the same time, the family learned that he had been injured. “For days, I did not know whether my son was still alive. The fact that former prisoners came forward as eyewitnesses gave us at least a little hope. I never gave up searching for him,” Adil Aslan said.




By late April, evidence increasingly suggested that Polad was being held captive by HTS. The family hired a lawyer in Damascus and is

author: Unknown
title: Iran launches drone attack on Azadî Camp in Koye
content:
Iran has once again carried out a drone attack on the Azadî Camp in the Koye district of the province of Hewlêr (Erbil) in southern Kurdistan (northern Iraq). It is not yet known whether anyone was injured or killed or what damage was caused.




The camp is home to members of the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I) and their families. Since the beginning of the war between Iran, the United States, and Israel, the camp has been targeted dozens of times by drone and missile attacks.




Other Rojhilat parties and their facilities in southern Kurdistan have also repeatedly been targeted by Iranian drone and missile strikes. Bases and camps belonging to the Komala factions and Sazmanî Xebat have been particularly affected.

author: Unknown
title: Botan: Disarmament is a precondition for peace, not peace itself - Part One
content:
Politician Lezgin Botan said that disarmament alone is not sufficient to resolve the Kurdish question, stressing that a lasting solution requires democratisation, legal reforms and guarantees for the political and cultural rights of Kurds.




The current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process has raised expectations among the Kurdish public regarding the direction and scope of the process and the steps to be taken next. Alongside discussions centred on security and disarmament, how to address the political, legal and social dimensions of the Kurdish question has also become a prominent issue.




Politician Lezgin Botan spoke to ANF about how the process is viewed by the Kurdish public, political and legal expectations, the relationship between disarmament and democratisation, and possible developments in the coming period.




Botan said that addressing the Kurdish question solely in terms of security and armed conflict was insufficient to explain all its dimensions, stressing the need to consider its political, social, legal and cultural aspects together.




Botan said: “Of course, ending armed conflict and removing weapons from the equation are important. However, it would be wrong to equate this with the Kurdish question itself. We must also distinguish between the concepts of ‘Terror-Free Turkey’ and the ‘Peace and Democratic Society Process’. The former can b

author: Unknown
title: Utamara Women's Foundation celebrates its 20th anniversary
content:
The Utamara Women's Foundation celebrated its 20th anniversary on 10 October at the Utamara Meeting Centre. The event brought together numerous women from different nationalities, as well as representatives of Germany's Social Democratic Party (SPD), the Greens and the Left Party, alongside equal opportunities officers from Neuwied and surrounding areas.







 







The programme began with opening speeches by the foundation's board members and staff, followed by discussions of Utamara's work, experiences and projects over the past two decades. A video documenting the foundation's history and activities was also screened.




Equal opportunities officers and the mayor who addressed the gathering highlighted Utamara's importance in the region. They stressed that the foundation had provided counselling and support to numerous women over the years and implemented various projects aimed at empowering women and promoting gender equality.




Utamara has served as a meeting place and centre of solidarity and support for women from diverse backgrounds for two decades, working to strengthen women's participation in social life and foster solidarity among them.




The celebration continued with a buffet featuring traditional dishes and live music. Participants shared their experiences and celebrated the foundation's 20th anniversary together.

author: Unknown
title: Özsoy: The state still takes a tactical approach to the Kurdish question
content:
The future of the Peace and Democratic Society Process continues to be debated, with the issue occupying an important place not only in Turkey's domestic political landscape but also in regional developments and international diplomacy. Dr. Hişyar Özsoy spoke to ANF about the political and diplomatic dimensions of the process, assessing how the state's approach, regional dynamics and the positions of international actors could influence its next stages.




Özsoy said the government was deliberately proceeding as slowly as possible with the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




Özsoy said: “The government is moving this process forward as slowly as possible. It takes considerable pressure before it makes even a small move. Only then does it take a minor step, after which the process appears to reach another deadlock. The government is trying to move forward while keeping control over the pace and substance of the process firmly in its own hands. So far, the process has advanced largely thanks to the patient and persistent steps taken by the Kurdish side.”




Özsoy said the state would take regional and international developments into account when determining the pace of the process. He explained how these developments could influence its calculations: “There are elections ahead in Israel and the United States. They may want to see how the regional cards are reshuffled, whe

title: Women’s delegation from North Kurdistan visits YPJ in Rojava
content:
During their visit to Rojava, a women's delegation from North Kurdistan visited institutions in Hesekê and the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ). The delegation met with institutional representatives, administrators, and commanders.




The delegation included Devrim Demir, the ousted co-mayor of Mardin Metropolitan Municipality and co-spokesperson of the Local Governments Diplomacy Committee; Safiye Akdağ, co-mayor of Yenişehir Municipality; Sevim Biçici, co-mayor of Silvan (Farqîn) Municipality; Belkıza Beştaş Epözdemir, co-mayor of Tatvan (Tetwan) Municipality; and Ruken Demir, a member of the Local Governments Diplomacy Committee.




Visit to the people's municipality




The delegation was welcomed at the Hesekê People’s Municipality by its co-mayors, Seidiye Kotî and Selman El Himêdî. The meeting continued behind closed doors. Afterward, the delegation presented the municipality with a commemorative plaque.




The North Kurdistan Women’s delegation also visited the Institution for Family and People’s Affairs, where it met with the institution’s director, Rohat Xelîl, and the deputy director.




Meeting with YPJ commanders




The delegation concluded its visit programme with a visit to the YPJ. YPJ Commander Newroz Ehmed, YPJ Spokesperson Rûksen Mihemed, and a group of fighters welcomed the delegation.

title: SOHR calls for the release of young men arbitrarily abducted from Afrin to Turkey eight years ago
content:
In a statement issued on Saturday, the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR) confirmed that the Turkish state had released four Kurdish men whom it had abducted from Afrin approximately eight years ago. The Observatory said that other people detained in the village and surrounding areas continue to be held in prisons in Turkey.




According to SOHR’s statement, in August 2018, Turkish civilian police, accompanied by intelligence officers, detained 13 young men from the village of Omar Uşaqî in the Afrin region and one person from a nearby village, on the allegation that they had links to the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria.




The detainees were reportedly first held in a school in their village, where they were beaten and subjected to torture, before being transferred to a school in a neighbouring village. SOHR also reported that large sums of money were demanded from their families before the men were transferred to Samsun Prison in Turkey.




At a trial held in Hatay on 12 December 2019, 11 of the detainees were sentenced to various prison terms, including life imprisonment.




SOHR called on the Turkish authorities to disclose the fate of all Kurdish detainees from Rojava, investigate allegations of torture and ill-treatment, and review the sentences imposed. The Observatory also called for the release of those being held arbitrarily and for those

title: DBP Co-Chair Uçar: Lasting peace can be achieved through women’s active participation in the process
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) organized a women’s gathering in Dersim under the slogan “We Are Building the Language of Peace.” The gathering, attended by numerous women as well as representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, addressed the role of women in the peace process and the importance of organized struggle.




Speaking at the gathering, DEM Party Dersim MP Ayten Kordu emphasized the importance of women’s organization, stating that women should be at the heart of the peace process.




Kordu said they would continue their efforts to broaden the scope of the Gülistan Doku case and stressed that women should participate more actively in the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




DBP Co-Chair Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar stated that peace cannot be addressed solely over the relationship of Kurds and Alevis with the state.




Emphasizing that the state must also make peace with women, workers, and nature, Uçar criticized attempts to limit the process to political alliances.




Describing the discussion of the Kurdish issue in the Grand National Assembly of Turkey as a historic turning point, Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar said, “So who brought these parties together? You did. Mr. Öcalan is the politician who has spoken most clearly and offered a perspective on peace and democracy.”




Uçar added, “When we talk about negotiations, it is our struggle that wi

author: Unknown
title: Guerrillas: We will continue our struggle until Leader Öcalan gains physical freedom
content:
Guerrillas from the HPG (People's Defense Forces) and YJA-Star (Free Women's Troops) spoke to ANF on the occasion of the 29th anniversary of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan on October 9, 1998. Forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country, the Kurdish leader went through a months-long odyssey through various countries before he was taken captive in the Kenyan capital Nairobi and handed over to Turkey on 15 February 1999. He has been incarcerated in İmralı Island Prison since and has not been seen his conditions improved despite the ongoing peace and democratic society process.




‘Leader Apo foiled the conspiracy through his resistance’




HPG guerrilla Azad Herekol began his remarks by condemning the international conspiracy and commemorated with respect and gratitude those who set themselves on fire in the “You Cannot Darken Our Sun” protests in response to the imprisonment of the Kurdish leader.




Emphasizing that the conspiracy against Öcalan aimed to destroy the Kurdish people and the peoples of the Middle East, Azad Herekol said the following: “The dominant powers knew very well that the struggle of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] was not only for one people, but for all oppressed societies. That is why they feared Leader Apo’s ideas and resorted to such a method. The international conspiracy involved not only impe

title: Gravestones of Kurdish martyrs buried en masse in a pit in Cudi region
content:
The Cuma Bilika and Binevş Edessa Martyrs’ Cemetery, where PKK members are buried in the village of Sipîndarok on the slopes of Mount Cudi in Şırnak, was destroyed in a bombing in 2015. Visits to the cemetery have since been prevented on the grounds that the area is a “military security zone.”




Cîhan Zîlan (Hatice Erbağ), who is buried in the cemetery, was killed in a clash in Cudi on March 31, 2006. Her brother Faysal Erbağ, who had been searching for her grave for 20 years, and his wife Bilmez Erbağ spotted her gravestone in footage previously recorded by the Mezopotamya Agency (MA). They subsequently traveled approximately 1,500 kilometers from Bursa to Cudi to reach the cemetery. The family was accompanied by the Şırnak Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture with Families Who Lost Their Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER).




During the visit, it was discovered that gravestones had been buried en masse in a pit dug near the cemetery’s parking area. Following rainfall, some of the gravestones have surfaced.




Denouncing the burial of the gravestones, MEBYA-DER Şırnak executive Fahrettin Salgucak said: “The stones caught our attention at the entrance to the cemetery. When we looked, we saw gravestones with names written on them. A pit had been dug here and the gravestones had been buried in it. With the rainfall, the stones have resur

title: International Conference on EU, Turkey and Kurds to take place 14-15 October
content:
The 20th International Conference on the EU, Turkey and the Kurds, organised by the EU Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC) in cooperation with The Left Group, the Greens/European Free Alliance, and the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament will take place on 15 October at the European Parliament in Brussels. On the evening of 14 October 2026, the EUTCC will host a special reception to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the conference series. 




Over the past twenty years, the EUTCC’s annual conferences have become an important forum for discussion on the Kurdish question, democracy, human rights, and prospects for peace in Turkey and the wider region. Bringing together academics, policy-makers, parliamentarians, civil society organisations, activists, and representatives of Kurdish and Turkish communities, these conferences have attracted significant political and media attention across Europe and beyond.




The program is as follows: 




Wednesday, 14 October, 17.00-19.00 Reception at Asp 00 Le Gran Cafe Spinelli

Thursday 15 October, 9.30-10.30

title: Message from the mountains of Kurdistan to the 39th International Women’s Gathering in Argentina
content:
The 39th International Women’s Gathering, bringing together thousands of women from different regions of Abya Yala, has begun in Córdoba, Argentina. During the three-day gathering, women will share their experiences through meetings and various activities and discuss strategies for advancing their struggles.




Ahead of the opening, members of the Kurdish Women’s Movement conveyed their greetings to the participants and also to Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who has been incarcerated in İmralı Island since 1999. A video message sent from the mountains of Kurdistan was then screened.




Speaking on behalf of KJAR (The Community of Free Women of Eastern Kurdistan) and the Kurdish Women’s Movement, Zîlan Vejîn greeted the 39th International Women’s Gathering and emphasized the importance of the common struggle.




Zîlan Vejîn stressed that Abdullah Öcalan’s philosophy offers an answer for peoples and women around the world.







 








The video message was enthusiastically received by the participants with great enthusiasm and slogans such as “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom].




Before the beginning of the three-day gathering, a ritual, according to the traditions of different original people of Abya Yaha, was held. The gathering’s activities will continue over the next two days, with the participation of women from across Abya Yala, representing various femin

author: Unknown
title: Unknown assailants vandalize the facility of the Families of Martyrs in Til Temir
content:
In the northeastern Syrian town of Til Temir, a facility belonging to the Council of Families of Martyrs was attacked and damaged by unknown assailants. The perpetrators tore down the sign bearing the council’s name and set a fire on the roof of the building. It is not yet known who was behind the attack.




The Council of Families of Martyrs, which organizes the relatives of members of the Kurdish freedom movement and the YPG/YPJ defense forces who have fallen in combat, issued a statement condemning the attack.




The Council stated that the attack violated the sanctity of the site and its moral and humanitarian significance. It called for the circumstances surrounding the incident to be clarified, those responsible to be identified and held accountable under the law.




The Council also called for the necessary measures to be taken to protect civil and social institutions in order to prevent such attacks from recurring.

title: Mehmed Uzun commemorated in Amed on 19th anniversary of his death
content:
On Sunday, relatives, companions, and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations gathered at the grave of Kurdish writer Mehmed Uzun in Mardinkapı Cemetery in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) to mark the 19th anniversary of his death on October 11, 2007. The commemoration, organized by the Association of Kurdish Writers, paid tribute to Uzun’s contribution to the development of modern Kurdish literature and his commitment to the Kurdish language.




His brother, Mustafa Uzun, thanked those present for attending. Mehmet Ildoğan, who had met the writer in Adıyaman, recalled how Uzun had inspired him and many others to develop a passion for literature. “We have only one Mehmed Uzun, not twenty,” Ildoğan said. “His works will light our way like a torch.”




Writing against language bans and cultural oppression




Herdem Merwani, co-chair of the Association of Kurdish Writers, described Uzun as one of the pillars of Kurdish literature. He said the association would continue its efforts to preserve and further develop this literary heritage.




Adem Avcı, the doctor who cared for Uzun during his battle with cancer, also paid tribute to his life’s work. He recalled that Uzun had fallen ill while in exile and had wanted to spend the final years of his life in his homeland. Avcı called on Kurdish writers to preserve Uzun’s legacy.

author: Unknown
title: Renewed ISIS attack in Hawija
content:
In recent days, ISIS militants have stepped up their activities in several areas and resumed attacks on Iraqi army forces along the border between the provinces of Kirkuk and Salahaddin.




Late last night, ISIS militants attacked an Iraqi army checkpoint in the village of Bur Xeliye, in the town of Denaniş on the outskirts of Hawija district in Kirkuk province.




Heavy clashes broke out between the two sides, and the militants were ambushed by security forces as they retreated. A number of militants were killed and wounded, while others managed to escape.




This was the third such attack carried out by ISIS militants along the same line.

author: Unknown
title: Tree felling by village guards in Besta
content:
Uninterrupted tree felling has been ongoing for seven years in the Cûdî and Gabar mountains and the Besta region. As a result of this ecological devastation, a large part of the Besta region has been left barren.




Hundreds of trees have reportedly been cut down in the Çemê Tahlo area.




It has been learned that the trees are being felled by village guards brought to the area from Hosyan village, in the Pervari (Berwarî) district of Siirt (Sêrt).

author: Unknown
title: Armed attack on Rojava FM team in Hesekê
content:
An armed attack was carried out against the Rojava FM team in the Salihi neighborhood of Heseke. One radio worker was injured, and the attackers reportedly stole a vehicle belonging to the team.




The injured worker was taken to hospital and is said to be in good condition following surgery.




The Internal Security Forces have launched an investigation into the attack.

title: Sustam: Those who sow insecurity reap revolt in France - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to Associate Professor Engin Sustam, a sociologist at Paris 8 University, about the causes of the student protests in France, their connection to the tradition of struggle stretching from 1968 to the present, and their potential to develop into a broader social opposition movement. 




Part one of this interview can be read 

here

. 




France has a strong tradition of student and youth movements stretching from 1968 to the present. Where do you place today’s mobilization within this historical continuity? What distinguishes it from previous student movements?




Of course, we can place this mobilization, the involvement of high school students and the forms of protest within a historical context. The 1968 movement, as we know, began primarily in universities rather than high schools. The Sorbonne and later Paris 8 University, as a different kind of experience, became important centres of this process. We should not forget that there was a broader dynamic of revolt across the world at the time.




There was the Vietnam War and the protests against it, anti-militarist movements, as well as workers’ strikes that intensified with the transition to the post-industrial era after the Second World War and struggles against social injustice. The 1968 movement emerged within this context. Today, however, we are dealing with a different context.
