title: Mining project in Kasor could trigger landslides and earthquakes, says report
content:
An expert report has been submitted to the case file in a lawsuit concerning the “Mineral Exploration Project Using Trenching and Drilling Methods,” planned by Kılıç Kardeşler Mining Construction Engineering and Project Services Industry and Trade Limited Company in the Kasor Basin, in the Kulp (Pasur) district of Diyarbakır (Amed). The report stated that the project area is classified as pastureland and lies within the Long-Distance Protection Zone of the Silvan Dam, highlighting various risks related to water resources, air emissions, landslides, erosion and biodiversity.




The expert report, prepared following an on-site inspection on 17 July 2026, stated that the environmental assessments and proposed measures for the project lacked sufficient technical justification across several areas of expertise.




An expert examination was conducted as part of a lawsuit filed before the Diyarbakır 1st Administrative Court seeking the annulment of the decision that an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was not required. During the site inspection, the expert panel heard the parties' arguments, conducted observations and examinations of the project area, took photographs and documented its findings in the report.




The examinations carried out by experts from different fields concluded that the environmental assessments and proposed measures outlined in the project introduction

title: Parlak: Framework Law must be formalized without delay
content:
As the process, brought into a new phase by the Call for Peace and a Democratic Society announced publicly by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025, approaches its second year, attention has shifted to the practical steps to be taken following the adoption of the framework law by Parliament.




The Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration was adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey on 10 August 2026, with 467 votes in favour. The bill stipulated that certain provisions could be implemented only after assessments by security institutions and confirmation of those assessments through a decision by the National Security Council (MGK).




Following the adoption of the framework law, a Monitoring and Evaluation Board and related bodies were established under the Presidency. Discussions continue over how to advance the process through lasting measures that build confidence.




DEM Party MP for Hakkari (Colemêrg), Vezir Coşkun Parlak, spoke to ANF about the process.




‘The National Security Council must fulfil its historic responsibility’




Parlak said that the overwhelming majority of MPs who voted in favour of the framework law had assumed a historic responsibility, and that the National Security Council (MGK) must demonstrate the same sense of responsibility. He added: “Just as the large majority in the Turkish Grand National Assembly that voted

title: Beşli: Laz and Kurdish peoples fell victim to the same state mentality
content:
Laz Culture Association President and lawyer Mehmedali Barış Beşli said social peace in Turkey cannot be limited simply to an end to conflict.




Beşli said the Laz and Kurdish peoples have historically fallen victim to the same state mentality and stressed the importance of resolving the Kurdish question for Turkey. He said,  “Resolving this bleeding wound of our country is, above all else, extremely important.”




Beşli said building social peace requires a democratic legal order in which different peoples and identities can live together on the basis of equal citizenship.




Laz Culture Association President and lawyer Mehmedali Barış Beşli spoke to ANF.




What does “social peace” mean to you?




Social peace, for us, does not simply mean silencing the guns or a state of non-conflict; it means establishing the rule of law, justice and the principle of equal citizenship. As the Laz Culture Association, we believe social peace is possible only if the state establishes an equal relationship with all identities on a constitutional basis. Social peace is possible when the ethnic identities of the people of Turkey can coexist in both the public and private spheres, and when society as a whole regards this coexistence as a value.

title: Çelik: No budget’ for students’ demands, yet 7.4 billion TL transferred to foundations
content:
As universities begin the autumn semester of the 2026–2027 academic year, a student at Istanbul Technical University (ITÜ) was expelled from a dormitory run by the Credit and Dormitories Institution (KYK) on the grounds that they had failed to pass the preparatory year in a single semester. With nowhere to stay, the student was forced to take refuge in the university library for days. They are now trying to continue their education while working to support themselves.




The experience of the ITÜ student is one example of the problems faced by thousands of students who are forced to work to continue their education, only to be labelled academically unsuccessful as a result and deprived of their right to housing.




Being a university student in Turkey is increasingly becoming less an educational experience and more a struggle for survival. The monthly scholarship or student loan of 4,000 TL (some 73 euros) provided to undergraduate students by the Ministry of Youth and Sports is not even enough to cover their basic needs, particularly in the face of rental prices and living costs in major cities.




Students forced working while studying




Rapidly rising rents for private dormitories and apartments in major cities have made KYK dormitories virtually the only housing option for students. Unable to receive sufficient financial support from their families due to the deepening

title: KNK calls for urgent action against environmental destruction in Southern Kurdistan
content:
The Environmental Commission of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) has strongly condemned the systematic destruction of forests and natural habitats by the Turkish military in Southern Kurdistan. In view of the ongoing deforestation in the Turkish-occupied border regions, it is calling for international investigations and decisive action by the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG). The commission described the destruction as ecocide aimed at permanently destroying Kurdistan’s natural foundations of life.




Satellite images document forest destruction




The statement comes in response to recent reports on the scale of environmental destruction in Duhok province. Comparisons of satellite images from twenty areas document changes in forest cover between 2013 and 2023. Particularly affected are the mountainous regions around Zaxo and Amêdî in Behdînan, where forests have been cleared and roads and military bases constructed in the course of the Turkish occupation. The images illustrate the extent to which the Turkish military presence has altered the landscape. In addition to the clearing of large forest areas, the transport of timber to Turkey and the destruction of other natural habitats have repeatedly been documented.




Kurdistan’s identity is being erased

author: Unknown
title: Seriously ill prisoners Orak and Karsu must be released
content:
The Prison Commission of the Istanbul branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) held the 759th of its weekly “F Sitting” protests in front of the association’s building in Beyoğlu.




The protest highlighted the health condition of Abdulhalik Orak (52), an ill prisoner held in Kırıkkale F-Type Prison. Attended by numerous human rights defenders, the demonstration featured a banner reading “Release ill prisoner Abdulhalik Orak”, while slogans were chanted including “Release ill prisoners”, “Treatment is a right and cannot be obstructed” and “Isolation kills, solidarity keeps people alive”.




The Initiative for Freedom for Sick Prisoners also gathered on Sakarya Street in Ankara for the 631st week of its protests. The demonstration drew attention to the health condition of seriously ill prisoner Botan Karsu, who is being held in Van High-Security Closed Prison.

author: Unknown
title: Protest against drugs in Şirnak
content:
The Şirnak Democratic Institutions Platform issued a press statement to draw attention to the increasing use of drugs and substance addiction.




Representatives of political parties, democratic mass organisations and many others attended the press conference, which was held on Sanat Street in the Silopi (Silopya) district of Şirnak. A banner reading “We are determined to combat drug use” was displayed, and the press statement was read out by Ziynet Şimşek, a member of the Silopi Municipality Council.




Saying that the rise in drug use and substance addiction in the city was a serious problem affecting all society, Ziynet Şimşek added: “One of society’s most significant problems in recent times has been the increase in drug use and substance addiction. We therefore need to address this issue seriously and take the right steps to resolve it.




Substance addiction is not a problem limited to those who use these substances. It affects families, young people, children and society as a whole. The oppression and exploitation of women and children are also connected to this problem. Furthermore, the widespread availability of drugs not only harms individuals’ health but also affects society’s safety, peace and future. This situation poses a serious problem, particularly for our young people and the future of our society.”

author: Unknown
title: Bayındır: The only way to bring this process to success is to organise and unite
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) held a public meeting in the Alucar neighbourhood of the Karayazı (Qereyazî) district of Erzurum under the slogan “We are building the promise of peace with the people”. DBP Co-Chair Keskin Bayındır, Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Colemêrg MP Onur Düşünmez and many others attended the meeting.




Keskin Bayındır said that, for the first time in history, a Kurdish movement had held official-level talks with the state over its own status, demonstrating that the Kurds had become a force. He continued: “That is why, despite all the uncertainty and concerns, we are not afraid of negotiations. Just as we were not afraid 45–50 years ago when we rose up in the mountains against oppression, today we are not afraid to sit at the negotiating table. From now on, we will continue our struggle through democratic politics, taking it into a new phase in accordance with the spirit and requirements of this new process.”




Bayındır added: “We are following all the statements being made. Some people comment that ‘the Kurds have abandoned the struggle’, either because they do not understand the situation or because they approach it with hostility. Yet, at the stage we have reached today, the Kurdish people have established their existence beyond any ambiguity. The fundamental issues before us now are our freedom and our status. From this poin

title: Demonstrations in Europe demand freedom for Abdullah Öcalan
content:
Protests were held in cities across Europe to mark the anniversary of the 9 October International Conspiracy. Through marches, rallies and public information campaigns, Kurds and their supporters protested the international conspiracy and raised their voices for Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom.




DÜSSELDORF




A mass press statement and march were held in Düsseldorf, Germany, under the leadership of the European Kurdish Women’s Movement. Kurds and their supporters gathered outside Düsseldorf Central Station (Hauptbahnhof), chanting slogans including “Bê Serok Jiyan Nabe” (Life Without a Leader Is Impossible), “Bijî Serok Apo” (Long Live Leader Apo) and “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom). Alongside photographs of Leader Apo, demonstrators carried banners and placards demanding his freedom.




Before the press statement, a group of Iranian individuals reportedly attempted to provoke tensions at the gathering. The situation was calmed after representatives of the democratic Kurdish organisations organising the event intervened, while German police removed the group from the area.







 







The statement began with the Kurdish national anthem, “Ey Reqîb”, followed by a minute of silence. Ehmed Kobanê, Co-Chair of the NRW Federation, and Ayten Kaplan, speaking on behalf of the European Kurdish Women’s Movement, then addressed the crowd.

content:
Three people were injured in an armed attack in the city of Hesekê.




According to information received, three people travelling in a vehicle through the Sînaa Junction were targeted by armed individuals. The injured civilians were taken to Reca Hospital.




Following attacks on public and private buildings and Kurdish symbols in the city, protests began in the Xiwêran neighbourhood.

title: Journalists Mustafa Balcı and Şaban Sevinç arrested
content: Mustafa Balcı and Şaban Sevinç, who were detained as “suspects” on “disinformation” charges as part of the funding investigation, were referred to a criminal court of peace following questioning by the prosecutor’s office. Balcı and Sevinç were arrested on charges of “publicly disseminating misleading information.”

title: Sustam: Those who sow insecurity reap revolt in France - Part One
content:
Student protests that began in high schools in France over educational conditions, staff shortages and deepening inequalities have spread to universities. The protests, which are continuing in many cities, particularly Paris and its suburbs, have brought into view not only discontent with the education system but also young people’s anger over a lack of prospects, poverty and social inequality.




Police interventions and far-right rhetoric criminalizing students have also reignited debates in France over security policies, racism and hostility towards migrants.




ANF spoke to Associate Professor Engin Sustam, a sociologist at Paris 8 University, about the causes of the student protests in France, their connection to the tradition of struggle stretching from 1968 to the present, and their potential to develop into a broader social opposition movement.




How do you assess the student protests that have spread from high schools to universities across France in recent weeks? What are the main social and political dynamics behind this movement?




For several months now, students across France, particularly high school students, have significantly expanded their protests and taken part in blockades, especially in Paris and its major suburbs, as well as in Bordeaux, Lyon and many other areas. High school students have even confronted the police much more forcefully, perhaps mo

author: Unknown
title: Mother tongue, identity and collective memory
content:
The mother tongue is more than the first language through which a person begins to discover the world. It is a bridge through which identity takes shape, a sense of belonging is established and collective memory is passed down through generations. From the language in which a child begins their education to the language in which a person can express themselves when receiving healthcare, the mother tongue encompasses far more than a purely cultural debate. Restricting the use of a language, excluding it from education or denying it a place in public life undoubtedly affects an individual's relationship with themselves and society.




People first learn to make sense of the world through the relationships around them. Alongside family and social relationships, language becomes part of this initial process of understanding. Sometimes, the first word a person learns is more than a means of communication; it becomes part of their connection to their family, their past and the community to which they belong.




Psychologist Siyabend Aslan defines the mother tongue as “the first home into which a person is born when they open their eyes to the world.” Aslan spoke to ANF about the place of language in human life, saying, “Rather than simply being an ordinary tool for communicating with the outside world, it lies at the very heart of our identity, our past and our sense of belonging.”

title: PYD calls for unity and restraint amid tensions in Hesekê
content:

The PYD stressed that the rise in hate speech and provocations in the region threatens internal peace, emphasising the need to clarify the circumstances surrounding the incidents and hold those responsible to account.




Syria needs a democratic and pluralistic system




The statement noted that Syria is passing through a sensitive and important transitional period. It said that all political and social forces must fulfil their national and historical responsibilities, strengthen dialogue among all of Syria’s communities and work to build trust.




The statement also stressed that steps had recently been taken to make progress on implementing the 29 January Agreement. It said these steps would contribute to strengthening stability, unifying efforts and building a democratic Syria.




‘Hate speech and provocations threaten internal peace’

title: Memorial in Argentina for Martyr Lêgerîn Çiya
content:
A meeting was held on Friday at 

Espacio de Alina

, in the mountains near Córdoba in Argentina. The space was established to keep the memory of Martyr Lêgerîn Çiya (Alina Sánchez) alive and strengthen solidarity among women.




The meeting was attended by feminist groups, indigenous women and comrades from the Kurdish women’s movement. Participants discussed political developments in Abya Yala and the dangers posed by the spread of fascism.







 








Through her struggle and resistance, Martyr Legerin Ciya succeeded in building bridges between Abya Yala, where she grew up, and the Kurdish movement she chose to join, said participants, adding that "she serves as an example and a guide not only within the Kurdish liberation movement but also within many feminist movements in Latin America, particularly in Argentina. The Alina Space, built in the mountains near the city of Córdoba in her memory, aims to become one of the physical places where this connection is forged. Various feminist and women’s collectives participated in the construction—including the physical building—of this space, using natural and traditional materials and methods."

title: Lawyer Çimen: Public power used to cover up Gülistan Doku case
content:
New developments have emerged in recent months in the investigation into the disappearance of Munzur University student Gülistan Doku, who went missing in Dersim on 5 January 2020. Numerous suspects have been detained or arrested as part of the investigation, while new digital records, witness statements and evidence have been added to the case file.




The number of people arrested in the investigation reached 38 in September, but questions surrounding Gülistan Doku's disappearance remain unanswered, and her family's pursuit of justice continues.




Ali Çimen, one of the lawyers representing Gülistan Doku's family, spoke to ANF about the latest developments in the investigation.




‘The case was systematically covered up’




Lawyer Ali Çimen said six waves of operations had been carried out in the Gülistan Doku case, with legal action taken against approximately 78 people and 38 arrested.




Çimen said the investigation had been ongoing for nearly seven years and that organised efforts had been made to cover up the case from the outset. He explained that they had faced serious difficulties in obtaining certain evidence, particularly because digital data had been deleted over time.

title: Internationalist youth delegation applies to meet Öcalan
content:
Members of the Diplomacy Commission of the Youth Assembly of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), together with an internationalist youth delegation from eight countries, submitted an application to the Ministry of Justice to meet with Abdullah Öcalan. The delegation made a statement at DEM Party headquarters following the application, expressing support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process and stressing the importance of Öcalan's freedom.




The delegation included representatives of Contre-Attaque & Autonomie from Switzerland, Sindacato Unione Democrazia Dignità Cobas from Italy, the Prosfygika Squatted Houses Community on Alexandras Avenue from Greece, La Saó from Catalonia, Mala Zêrîn from Austria, Jeunesse Internationaliste Française from France, Cumann Saol Saor from Ireland, and the Democratic Youth Union (YUNA) from Germany.




The statement was read in English by YUNA member Isabelle Marie Whittenberg and in Turkish by DEM Party Youth Assembly member Jiyan Bahadır.




‘The Peace and Democratic Society Process is a historic opportunity’




Isabelle Marie Whittenberg said the delegation had come from European countries to support the Peace and Democratic Society Process. She said Abdullah Öcalan had been targeted by an international conspiracy 27 years ago and had been held on Imrali Island ever since.

title: Xerîb Hiso: Attempts are being made to provoke conflict between Kurds and Arabs in Hesekê
content:
As steps are being taken to implement the agreement signed on January 29 between the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria and the Syrian Interim Government, security incidents and provocations continue in the region. The incidents began with the killing of a member of the Internal Security Forces in Qamishlo and continued with an attack on a vehicle of security forces, the killing of Sîpan Hiznî, and developments in various areas, particularly Kobanê.




Most recently, groups gathered in the Xiwêran neighborhood of Hesekê and marched toward Kurdish neighborhoods and engaged in provocations. One member of the Internal Security Forces and three civilians were injured in the ensuing incidents.




PYD co-chair Xerîb Hiso spoke to ANF about the provocation in Hesekê.




'The racist mentality that denies the Kurds is active on the ground'

title: Jineolojî to determine roadmap for the new period
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference will be held in the Netherlands from October 16 to 18 under the slogan “Building a Communal and Free Life with Jineolojî.” Organized by members of the Jineolojî Academy and the European Jineolojî Committee, the conference will take place under the main theme “The Role of Jineolojî in Building a Democratic and Communal Life.”




The conference will assess the experience accumulated through more than a decade of Jineolojî work in Europe in the fields of women’s liberation struggle, alternative knowledge production, collective living practices, democratic education and communal solidarity. It also aims to further develop the role of Jineolojî in social construction and determine a roadmap for the period ahead.




The organizers said that the goal is to develop a shared perspective on the future of Jineolojî, which has generated significant knowledge and opened up new avenues in Europe and around the world over the past decade.




Jineolojî’s role in social construction to be discussed




As part of the conference, the ten years of experience accumulated through Jineolojî work in Europe will be assessed from historical, sociological and organizational perspectives. The role of Jineolojî in social construction and the organizational model for the new period will be discussed within the framework of a democratic and communal society.

title: Yüksel Aksu: We need equal citizenship and respect for identity
content:
Art in Turkey, particularly over the past fifty years, has been heavily influenced by militarist and fascist propaganda. Social issues, especially those concerning Kurds and the Kurdish question, have largely been portrayed in the arts through a militarist and dominant perspective.




Yüksel Aksu, one of the directors in Turkish cinema who has approached Kurds and the Kurdish question outside this dominant perspective, spoke to ANF about his approach to filmmaking and the role of art in the struggle for peace in Turkey.




Cinema gave me the opportunity to question the world




Aksu said he entered the world of cinema somewhat by chance and described how his journey began: “It happened somewhat by chance. Like many children growing up in small towns, I enrolled in a couple of university programmes that promised secure careers, but I was expelled from them. As the saying goes, every cloud has a silver lining. Around that time, the entrance exams for the cinema department at the Faculty of Fine Arts came up. I took the exam and was accepted. But I had always been drawn to storytelling, art, drama and fiction.

author: Unknown
title: HRANA: 2,003 people executed in Iran in one year
content:
On the occasion of the World Day Against the Death Penalty, the Human Rights Activists News Agency’s Statistics Center (HRANA) published its annual report on the use of the death penalty in Iran. The report highlighted a sharp increase in executions, continued secrecy surrounding the implementation of death sentences, and a rise in executions related to political and security charges.




HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran between 10 October 2025, and 8 October 2026, based on 1,857 reports. This represents an increase of approximately 29 percent compared with the previous reporting period. During the same period, the death sentences of 230 people were documented.




The report stated that one person was executed every four hours and 35 minutes, adding that 95 percent of executions were not announced by official sources.




By location, Razavi Khorasan recorded the highest number of executions, with 200, followed by Isfahan with 164 and Alborz with 123. There were 119 executions recorded in Fars, 112 in Khuzestan, and 102 in Lorestan.




At the prison level, Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan and Adelabad Prison in Shiraz recorded the highest numbers of executions.




The report added that 95 percent of documented executions were carried out in secret or without public announcement, while only 5 percent were reported by official and local sources.

content:

Representatives of political parties and civil society organisations, along with residents from the Karlıova (Kanîreş) and Yedisu (Çêrme) districts, attended a press statement organized by the Bongilan Ecology Platform. The statement emphasised the need to protect pastures and highland meadows.




Canfidal Boldaş, the Bingöl (Çewlîg) Provincial Secretary of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB), stated that implementing renewable energy projects in unsuitable locations causes environmental destruction. title: MP Öznur Bartın: Kurds are key actors in Turkey’s democratic future
content:
As parliament begins its new legislative term, the Peace and Democratic Society Process has also entered a new political phase. The role parliament will assume in the next stage of the process, the political will demonstrated by parties and society’s participation in the process of democratic resolution are coming to the fore.




ANF spoke to Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Hakkari (Colemerg) Öznur Bartın about expectations for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question, the scope of the framework law and the steps that need to be taken.




Bartın stressed that disarmament should be regarded as the beginning of democratic transformation and underlined the importance of securing constitutional and legal guarantees for the language, identity, culture and political rights of the Kurdish people.




‘Disarmament is not the end of the process, but the beginning of democratic transformation’




Bartın said the points on which different political parties have been able to find common ground in parliament during the Peace and Democratic Society Process are important, stressing that the process must move beyond disarmament.

title: Yıldırım: Sentence reductions have become a defence for femicide perpetrators
content:
In Kurdistan, where femicides are widespread alongside special warfare policies, the perpetrators may change, but the methods and defences used after the murders remain the same. Taking their cue from unjust provocation and good conduct sentence reductions granted by the judiciary, perpetrators research defences used in previous cases and make similar statements in court.




Recent femicide cases in Diyarbakır (Amed) have also revealed examples of this pattern. Arselan Akdemir, who murdered Sultan Kara, resorted to the defence, “I am mentally ill. I have a medical report,” while Cemal Alparaslan, who murdered İlayda Alkaş, appeared at his first hearing wearing a tie.







 







Derya Yıldırım, a member of the Board of Directors of the Diyarbakır Bar Association, drew attention to the impact of perpetrators' defences on judicial proceedings in femicide cases. She said sentence reductions granted on grounds such as unjust provocation, good conduct and mental health obscure the history of violence behind femicides.




Yıldırım said the defences used by perpetrators during judicial proceedings are increasingly becoming an established method. title: HPG and YJA Star guerrillas: The international conspiracy was foiled through struggle
content:
Today marks the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan. The process referred to as the international conspiracy, in which numerous nation-states were involved, began on October 9, 1998, when Öcalan was forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country. This was followed by a months-long odyssey through various countries, ending on February 15, 1999, with his abduction from the Kenyan capital Nairobi to Turkey. The Kurdish leader has been held on the prison island of Imrali ever since.




On the anniversary of the international conspiracy, guerrillas of the HPG (People’s Defense Forces) and YJA Star (Free Women’s Troops) spoke to ANF and expressed their views.




Democratic modernity against capitalist modernity

This was followed by the Leader’s journey to Greece, his departure from Greece for Russia, then his journey to Rome, his return to Russia, and ultimately a four-month process that ended with his captivity. content:

The KCK statement on Friday reads as follows:

title: Syriac homes in İdil demolished despite ongoing court proceedings
content:
The AKP-run municipal administration in the İdil district of Şırnak province is issuing demolition orders against homes and commercial premises belonging to members of the Syriac community. Four of the affected Syriac citizens have already initiated legal proceedings against the measures. Nevertheless, their buildings were demolished before the court could rule on their objections. Measures have also been taken against a guesthouse belonging to the Syriac Orthodox Church of the Virgin Mary. Those affected view the actions as an attempt to intimidate the Syriac community and weaken its ties to its homeland.




Demolitions despite legal objections




Lawyer Melke Karagöl, whose own family is affected by the demolition orders, criticized the municipal administration’s actions. The demolished buildings belonged to four Syriac residents and were between 20 and 25 years old. “Three days before the demolition, we filed an objection with the court. Before a decision had even been made, the houses were demolished,” Karagöl told MA. The court proceedings are still pending. However, the municipal administration created a fait accompli without waiting for the outcome.

title: Freedom for Öcalan Committee in Southern Kurdistan vows to continue its work without interruption
content:
The Committee for the Freedom of Abdullah Öcalan in Southern Kurdistan has called for intensified social and political efforts for the freedom of the Kurdish leader on the 28th anniversary of the international conspiracy of October 9, 1998.




In a written statement on Friday, the committee described the conspiracy as a systematic and ideological attack by hegemonic powers on the free will of society. It said the conspiracy was directed not only against a political organization, but against the vision of a democratic and self-determined society.




“As the creator of the philosophy of democratic society, Leader Öcalan, through his readings of historical truth and his dialectical insights into the crises of the contemporary world, has transformed the Imrali prison from a place of punishment into a center of thought and knowledge. The resistance of Leader Öcalan and the Freedom Movement has freed humanity from the violations of capitalist modernity and the tenets of the classical nation-state, advancing it toward a higher level of self-governance,” the statement said.




The Committee pointed out that Öcalan’s intellectual will could not be broken despite 27 years of isolation and psychological torture, while the ruling authorities have faced a multifaceted legal and moral collapse.

title: Ayşegül Doğan calls for the peace process to be accelerated, says legal changes are needed
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan spoke about her party’s ongoing Central Executive Board (MYK) meeting in Ankara on Friday.




Speaking at a press conference at the party headquarters, Ayşegül Doğan addressed the issues on their agenda.




Doğan first referred to the 28th anniversary of the October 9 international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan. She said that the conspiracy was aimed particularly at pitting the Kurdish and Turkish peoples against each other, undermining domestic peace in Turkey and making peace in the Middle East impossible.




“In its 28th year, this conspiracy must come to an end, which will only be possible if we achieve lasting peace,” she underlined.




‘We are facing a systemic crisis’




Pointing to the financial scandal in the country, Ayşegül Doğan stated: “What Turkey is facing is a serious issue that requires scrutiny of public oversight and political accountability. There is an obvious systemic crisis, and the economic crisis is deepening. Hunger, poverty, unemployment and indebtedness have reached historically high levels in Turkey. title: Women's delegation from North Kurdistan visits Rojava
content:
The women’s delegation from North Kurdistan visited the Martyr Xebat Dêrik Cemetery in the city of Dêrik together with the families of martyrs and laid carnations on the graves of the martyrs.




The delegation included Devrim Demir, co-mayor of Mardin Metropolitan Municipality, who was replaced by a state-appointed trustee, and co-spokesperson of the Local Governments Diplomacy Committee; Safiye Aladağ, co-mayor of Amed Yenişehir Municipality; Sevim Biçici, co-mayor of Silvan (Farqîn) Municipality; Belkize Beştaş Epözdemir, co-mayor of Tatvan Municipality; and Rûken Demir, a member of the Diplomacy Committee.




The delegation members drew attention to the sacrifices made by the martyrs and stated that they would continue to uphold their struggle. Following the cemetery visit, the delegation visited the Council of Martyrs’ Families in Dêrik.




Cooperation between local administrations discussed




Today, the women’s delegation met with Îlham Ehmed, co-chair of the Department of Foreign Relations of the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria, and Cîhan Hesam, director of the Qamishlo Region.




Speaking after the meeting, the delegation said that the purpose of the visit was to share the experiences of local administrations, strengthen cooperation between institutions, and explore ways to contribute to joint initiatives.

title: Key issues in integration with Damascus remain unresolved
content:
The integration process between the Damascus Interim Government and the Autonomous Administration in Syria has entered a new phase in the military sphere, while developments over the past month in particular have made uncertainties surrounding the political, social and cultural dimensions of the process more visible. Restrictions on Kurdish-language education and the protests against them, the killing of Hasakah (Hesekê) Brigade fighter Sîpan Hiznî, and people taking to the streets following the prison fire in Kobanê all occurred during the same period.




The new phase, which began with the announcement on 25 August that the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) would cease to exist as an independent military structure, is progressing with the incorporation of its fighters into the Syrian army. Steps are being taken to integrate the Kobanê Brigade into an Aleppo-based structure and the forces in Hasakah into the institutions of the Interim Government.




However, progress in military integration has not resolved questions about the future of the education, security, cultural and local government institutions that Kurds have built over the past 14 years. Discussions are continuing over the extent to which these institutions will be preserved and what status they will have in the new Syria.

title: ICOR: The YPJ cannot be eliminated through negotiations
content:
ICOR Women, the women’s section of the International Coordination of Revolutionary Parties and Organizations (ICOR), expressed support for the international solidarity campaign launched in April in support of the Kurdish Women’s Protection Units (YPJ).




ICOR Women said that the YPJ is not merely a military organization, but represents women’s right to self-defense, equality, and to determine their own social lives.




The statement said that for more than 13 years, the YPJ has represented women’s resistance to patriarchal violence and oppression, adding that Kurdish women’s struggle for freedom has served as an example to women around the world.




The statement also referred to the agreement signed between the Syrian government and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on January 29, 2026, saying that a new period has begun for the future of Syria and Rojava. However, it emphasized that in negotiations concerning the future of a new Syria, women’s participation in political, social, and military life must not be treated as a secondary issue.




“You cannot eliminate the YPJ through negotiations!” the statement said, describing the YPJ as representing self-determination, equality, and the protection of women from violence and oppression. title: Narges Mohammadi’s health deteriorates in Iranian prison
content:
The health of imprisoned Iranian human rights activist and 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has reportedly deteriorated.




Mohammadi, who has been under medical supervision in hospital for about a week due to a heart condition, is in increasingly poor health, according to new information shared by her lawyer.




Her lawyer said Mohammadi had lost 20 kilograms and was struggling to speak. The lawyer said, “She has difficulty speaking, and the appearance of her head and face has changed.”




‘Her health is deteriorating with every passing minute’




Mohammadi's lawyer said she was being held under tight security at a hospital in northeastern Iran, adding: “Her health is deteriorating with every passing minute.”




Human rights activists have demanded that Mohammadi be transferred as soon as possible to a fully equipped hospital in Tehran, where she can receive treatment from specialist medical teams.




Treatment in Tehran is being blocked




Narges Mohammadi, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023, was arrested in January 2025 during the funeral of lawyer Khosrow Ali Kordi in Mashhad and was subsequently sentenced to prison.




Mohammadi suffered a heart-related medical emergency at Zanjan Prison on 1 May. Her health has reportedly failed to improve since then and has continued to deteriorate.

title: KON-MED calls for demonstrations in five German cities against the international conspiracy
content:
The Confederation of Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED) has called for demonstrations and rallies in Düsseldorf, Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt and Bremen on Saturday, October 10. The occasion is the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan on October 9, 1998. The umbrella organization is demanding freedom for the Kurdish leader imprisoned in Turkey and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.




In a statement on Thursday, KON-MED described October 9, 1998, as the beginning of a new and decisive phase in the international conspiracy against the leader of the Kurdish freedom movement. On that date, Öcalan was forced to leave Syria. After a months-long odyssey through various countries, he was arrested in Kenya on February 15, 1999, and forcibly transferred to Turkey.




“These events made it clear that the Kurdish question does not concern Turkey alone, but that international powers are also directly involved,” the statement said. Even 28 years later, the developments of that period have lost none of their political significance, according to the Kurdish umbrella organization.

title: Hüseyin Olan: AKP uses all state resources for its own interests in Bitlis
content:
A long-running road problem in Aladana village in the Hizan district of Bitlis (Bedlîs) has pushed residents to the point of revolt.




Road repair work carried out by teams from the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration on the Horozdere Group Road has raised many questions after Aladana, a village largely inhabited by Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) voters, was left without asphalt.




DEM Party MP for Bitlis Hüseyin Olan spoke to ANF about the extent of the Justice and Development Party’s (AKP) partisanship in Bitlis and across Kurdistan. Olan said, “The AKP has now become a party-state. It uses all the resources of the state for its own interests and discriminates in the provision of services between those who vote for it and those who do not.”




‘AKP invests in villages where it receives the most votes in Bitlis’




The failure to asphalt the road to Aladana village, where most residents are the DEM Party voters, has sparked strong reactions during repair work on the Horozdere Group Road launched by the Special Provincial Administration in the Hizan district of Bitlis. While teams from the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration laid asphalt on the Horozdere Group Road, the entrance road to nearby Aladana was left unpaved, raising questions over the decision.

title: KJK: We should demand Öcalan’s freedom louder
content:

The global and regional alliance of international and regional powers that paved the way for the Kurdish genocide has gone down in history as one of the dirtiest and most dangerous alliances and conspiracies in the history of the Middle East and the world. Abdullah Öcalan, who was captured as the conspiracy unfolded, has been held under unprecedented conditions on Imrali Island for 28 years and has mounted an unparalleled resistance against these conditions and his captivity. We first salute Öcalan for this resistance, which enlightens us, strengthens us and guides us, and we renew our pledge and determination to bring the struggle for freedom and democracy to success along Öcalan’s path."




The KJK added: "Beginning on 9 October itself, thousands of our martyrs formed a circle of fire and blood around Öcalan in an effort to thwart this conspiracy. Throughout almost every day of this 28-year conspiracy, martyrs have been lost in all areas of our struggle. Each of our martyrs is a symbol and a great value of the struggle against this conspiracy. title: Kurdish Movement: There are no longer any obstacles for delaying steps regarding Öcalan’s freedom
content:
In a statement about the peace and democratic society process, the leadership of the Kurdish freedom movement announced further steps by its armed forces. According to the statement, the forces that had remained in Turkey until now have also been fully withdrawn in recent days. At the same time, four war tunnels and positions in Metîna, west of Zap, have been evacuated.




The Movement Leadership stated that this completes the implementation of the consequences arising from the decision to end the armed struggle against Turkey. Responsibility now lies with the political leadership in Ankara. In particular, there is no justification for any further delay regarding Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom, free working and communication conditions for the Kurdish leader, and further legislative measures, it underlined.




In its statement, the Movement Leadership also reviewed the course of the peace process to date, criticized the form of the framework law adopted in August, and called on social and democratic forces in Turkey to actively engage in the process.




The statement on Thursday reads as follows:




From the end of the armed struggle to a political solution

title: Berlin Twinning Association visits partner city Dêrik
content:
A delegation from the Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg–Dêrik Twinning Association has been visiting its partner city of Dêrik in Rojava since September 28. During meetings with the city’s new leadership and visits to schools, healthcare facilities and water projects, the focus has been both on political and administrative changes and on continuing the long-standing partnership.




At the beginning of the visit, the delegation met Dêrik’s new mayor, Mihemed, and her deputy, Carlos Kori. The discussions focused on the current integration process in Syria, changes to municipal structures and future cooperation with Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg. During an official reception, the delegation also met Şero Şero, who holds an important regional role as district governor.




“Reliable relationships at the municipal level are particularly important at a time when political and administrative structures are undergoing fundamental change,” said Janosch Tries, a board member of the Twinning Association.

title: Satellite images document ecological destruction in Southern Kurdistan
content:
Satellite images from twenty areas in the Duhok province in Southern Kurdistan (Northern Iraq)  document the extent of ecological destruction linked to the Turkish occupation. Comparisons of the images show how formerly forested mountain slopes were extensively cleared within just a few years and opened up by new roads. The regions of Zaxo and Amêdî, where the Turkish army has been expanding its military infrastructure for years, have been particularly affected, according to a report by the Mezopotamya News Agency (MA).




Particularly since the intensification of Turkish incursions into Zap, Avaşîn and Metîna in 2017, numerous roads and military bases have been constructed in the mountainous regions. Forest areas are cleared for their construction, fragmenting previously contiguous landscapes. At the same time, large quantities of timber have been transported from the affected areas to Turkey for years.




Deforestation in the mountainous regions of Behdînan




The Behdînan region, particularly the areas of Zaxo, Duhok, Berwarî Bala and Amêdî, has been especially severely affected. Deforestation there has once again intensified recently. According to research conducted on the ground, the companies involved are stepping up their operations ahead of winter. The felled trees are loaded onto trucks under military supervision and transported across the border into Turkey.

title: KHRN reports enforced disappearances of five Kurdish opposition figures in Iran
content:
The security agencies of the Islamic Republic of Iran, specifically the Ministry of Intelligence and the Intelligence Organization of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), have increasingly deployed enforced disappearance against members of Kurdish opposition groups since June 2025, following the outbreak of the 12-day Israel-Iran conflict, which also involved US military strikes.




At least five Kurdish political activists have since been subjected to enforced disappearance: Mohsen Ghaderi, Sara Rashidi Kachlanlou, Zahra Pirdehghan, Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Qizilbash and Sirwan Habibi. They were arrested in Baneh, Paveh, Orumiyeh, and Kamyaran, and subsequently subjected to enforced disappearance.




Despite credible eyewitness testimonies and evidence confirming their detention by Iranian government security forces, Iran’s judicial authorities have not formally registered their detention. Security agencies also continue to deny their families information about their whereabouts or custody status.




This situation places the detainees outside the protection of the law, depriving them of access to legal counsel, communication with their families and necessary medical care.




These enforced disappearances have emerged amid a shift in detention practices following the recent regional hostilities and the bombardment of several security facilities.

title: ISIS member apprehended in Hewler
content:
The Iraqi Federal Intelligence and Investigation Agency issued a statement regarding an operation carried out in Hewlêr in cooperation with the security forces of the Kurdistan Region.




The agency stated that an ISIS member considered to be a high-risk individual and subject to an arrest warrant under Article 4 of the Anti-Terrorism Law was apprehended in the operation in Hewler (Erbil) province.




A quantity of foreign currency, a passport and cards belonging to various banks were also reportedly seized from the ISIS member.




On Tuesday morning, a senior member of the jihadist group Islamic State (ISIS) was arrested following an attack on an Iraqi Federal Police base in Hawija. Two police officers were killed and several others injured in the attack on Monday.

title: KNK condemns the 9 October conspiracy, calls for freedom for Öcalan
content:
The Foreign Affairs Commission of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) released a statement condemning the international conspiracy that led to Abdullah Öcalan’s imprisonment, and once again expressing its support for his call for ‘peace and democratic society’.




The international conspiracy began on October 9, 1998, when Abdullah Öcalan was forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country. This was followed by a months-long odyssey through various countries, ending on February 15, 1999, with his abduction from the Kenyan capital Nairobi to Turkey. The Kurdish leader has been held on the prison island of Imrali ever since.




The KNK statement on Thursday reads as follows:

In the early 1990s, the U.S. launched a large-scale military intervention in the Middle East. Its aim was to reshape the region in line with its own interests. Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait on August 2, 1990, was the pretext the U.S. needed to rapidly increase its military presence in the region.

author: Unknown
title: The memory of the future
content:
Almost five hundred years ago, the eighteen-year-old Étienne de La Boétie wrote his 

Discourse on Voluntary Servitude

. This text, which asks how freedom is lost and how people can become accustomed to submission, is today assigned as reading to secondary school students in France.




Why do people submit?




La Boétie’s answer, which continues to preoccupy us to this day, is not solely about tyranny. The first generation may still be subjugated by force. But subsequent generations, born under the yoke and having never known freedom, may begin to regard the order into which they were born as the natural condition of life. Habit, La Boétie argues, teaches people to “swallow the poison of servitude without finding it bitter.” It is then no longer merely a matter of submitting, but of drinking the poison and, after a while, no longer even realizing that it is poison.




An order established through violence can, over time, become a matter of habit. But another question makes La Boétie even more relevant to us today: Do people become accustomed only to their own subjugation, or can they also become accustomed to the injustice inflicted on the person right beside them? When we apply this question to Turkey and Kurdistan, we are confronted with a deeply burdensome history.

title: MSD on incidents in Heseke: The issues must be addressed through political and legal dialogue
content:
Following a demonstration featuring anti-Kurdish demands in Heseke, the Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) expressed deep concern over the recent developments and the growing tensions in the city.




At a rally in the predominantly Arab neighborhood of Xiwêran (Ghweiran) last Friday, around 200 people called, among other things, for Kurds to be removed from institutions in Hesekê province. During the demonstration, in which a particularly large number of children and young people participated, slogans were also chanted against Kurdish national symbols and flags. Kurdish flags were also reportedly burned following Friday prayers. 




“Statements and positions that could deepen ethnic and social divisions are particularly troubling in an area known for its diversity and the close ties among its communities, “MSD said in a statement on Thursday.




The MSD recognizes that residents of Heseke Governorate, regardless of their background, have legitimate concerns, demands, and rights, and they have the right to express them peacefully. These include calls for security, public services, effective state institutions, and political and administrative rights. Such concerns should be addressed through the law, dialogue, and the political process, not through accusations, exclusion, or incitement.

title: 12 prisoners begin hunger strike at Bukan prison
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Network reported that at least 12 Kurdish prisoners being held at Bukan Prison for political and religious reasons began a hunger strike on October 5 to protest pressure exerted by Iranian regime forces in prisons.




The prisoners announced in a letter to Bukan Prison authorities on 5 October that they had begun a hunger strike. They are reportedly protesting restrictions on their access to leave permits and the open-prison placement program, as well as restrictions imposed on them under prison conditions.




The prisoners whose names have been identified as participating in the hunger strike are: Ardalan Mineh, Behrouz Barakhas, Esmail Atash-Mard, Kaveh Rahimi, Hamed Maroufi, Ali Mohammadi, Mahmoud Jafari, Ali Faroughi, Arsalan Minaei, Aziz Banehei, Ghader Salimi, and Mullah Davoud.




It was reported that on the second day of the hunger strike, the 12 prisoners were transferred to the quarantine section on the orders of the director of Bukan Prison. Their phone calls and family visits are reportedly still being restricted.




A Kurd detained 




Meanwhile, Faramarz Seîdî, from the city of Dehgolan in Kurdistan Province, was detained by forces from the Ministry of Intelligence using violence and taken to a detention facility operated by the ministry. title: Women murdered in Amed: A common story of violence, complaints, and failed protection
content:
In the first eight months of 2026, 197 women were killed by men in Kurdistan and Turkey. The same period also saw suspicious deaths of women and cases in which women were driven to suicide.




In Diyarbakır (Amed), one woman has died under suspicious circumstances since June, while the body of another woman who disappeared years ago was also found. Four women were also killed by men during this period.




Similar circumstances emerged behind the suspicious deaths and femicides in the city, while the families of the women killed shared a common demand: penalties must be sufficiently deterrent.




Four women killed




Interviews with the families of the women killed during this period revealed that the women had been subjected to systematic violence and were not adequately protected despite reporting the abuse to the police.




Sultan Karadağ was killed on 10 August. Sultan Kara was killed on 26 August by Ersan Akdemir, whom she wanted to divorce. Mizgin Kılıç was killed on 18 September by her former husband, and Ayfer Çakmak was killed on 27 September by her husband Orhan Çakmak, after reportedly enduring systematic violence for years.




The names and number of the women killed are more than mere statistics. Although their stories differed, they shared a common experience: they were subjected to violence, and their requests for protection went unanswered.

title: KDP seeks permission from Turkey to use roads in its own territory
content:
Organizers of the Berwarî Bala Festival in Amêdiyê, linked to the KDP, and the KDP’s 18th Branch obtained permission from the Turkish state to use the roads for the event.




A source who spoke to Rojnews about the issue said that although the decision provides some relief to citizens and festival participants, it has also raised serious concerns and questions among local residents. The source said: “This is a public and tourist road within the Kurdistan Region. However, it has become an occupied and military road. Citizens have to obtain permission from the Turkish state to travel on this road in their own territory, and their passage is subject to conditions. This permission has been granted for only three days for the festival.”




According to information obtained, the road normally used to reach these areas is 35 kilometers long. However, for the past three days, people coming from outside the city who need to travel to Kanîmasî have been forced to use a route more than 80 kilometers long that is designated for local residents and villages. This situation places a significant burden on tourists and the local population.

title: Once again on Kurdish democratic unity
content:
The creation of Kurdish democratic unity continues to be a matter of urgent importance. The stage reached by the Third World War, which is spreading and deepening across the Middle East, makes this an immediate necessity. The process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan’s Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February 2025 has made Kurdish democratic unity an urgent task.




Although some collaborationist-nationalist circles continue to create obstacles, the forces supporting national democratic unity are growing by the day. Kurdish intellectuals and politicians are placing greater emphasis on democratic unity than ever before. Politicians are speaking about democratic unity, while intellectuals are writing about it. There is a demand both for unity and for that unity to be democratic, because the Kurds need both unity and democracy. At present, there is neither sufficient national unity nor sufficient democracy. Yet developments in the region and the struggle in Kurdistan need democratic unity more than bread and water.




The stage reached by the Third World War in the region is creating both significant opportunities for the Kurds and very serious dangers. To seize these opportunities and avert these dangers, the Kurds need to unite and develop their democracy. With Kurdish politics fragmented, lacking unity and democracy, it does not appear possible to seize these opportuni

title: Çetintepe: Constitutional Court ruling may leave women more helpless
content:
The Constitutional Court annulled on 4 June 2026 the provision in Article 175 of the Turkish Civil Code that allowed a spouse who would fall into poverty as a result of divorce to claim alimony from the other spouse “indefinitely,” finding it unconstitutional. The reasoning for the annulment was published in the Official Gazette on 30 September. The ruling will take effect nine months later, on 30 June 2027.




Gamze Çetintepe of the Women’s Defence Network spoke to ANF about the Constitutional Court’s ruling and drew attention to how the reasoning portrays men who pay alimony as “victims.” Çetintepe said women’s acquired rights were being taken away and women’s labour was being rendered invisible.




Çetintepe said the ruling was based on a narrative suggesting that women were trying to “take away” something that rightfully belonged to men and that this created a grievance for men.




Çetintepe described the ruling as part of propaganda aimed at trapping women in families marked by exploitation and violence, in line with the “Decade of the Family” policies of making divorce more difficult, encouraging marriage and increasing birth rates. She said the reasoning behind the ruling states:“The reasoning states: ‘Due to the contested provision, the obligation to pay poverty alimony may continue until the end of a person’s life, which could prevent that person from remarrying, ac

author: Unknown
title: Özmen: Municipalities should support Kurdish theatre
content:
Teatra Jiyana Nû (TJN), which holds an important place in Kurdish theatre, announced that it has resumed its work after a long break. The group opened the new season with the children’s play Rovî Ji Çiyê Xeyidîye and also announced that it is preparing a new play for adults.




Founded in 1992 within the Mesopotamia Cultural Centre (MKM), Teatra Jiyana Nû has staged many significant productions in Kurdish theatre over the years. The group has performed plays including Daweya Generale Teneke, Ta: Sê Evren Dûr and Komara Dinan: Şermola. Teatra Jiyana Nû later formed a subgroup called Şanoya Helîn, where it also provided acting training.




Teatra Jiyana Nû faced numerous bans and forms of repression throughout its years of activity. Its plays were repeatedly banned, its stages were sealed, and its actors were detained and arrested. Some actors from the group later joined the Kurdish Freedom Movement. The group’s most recent play, Berû, was also banned in many cities across Turkey and Kurdistan. The group suspended its activities for a long period following this process and is now returning to the stage with the new season.




Teatra Jiyana Nû, which opened the season with the children’s play Rovî Ji Çiyê Xeyidîye, will also launch a workshop to provide theatre training in the new period.

title: Sites of historical memory and peace: Sacred domes
content:
Yazidis (Êzidî) do not visit the domes only on special days, holidays and during religious rituals; they also regard these places as sites of spiritual peace and visit them in their daily lives.




Looking at when the domes were built, it becomes clear that each was constructed in some of the most beautiful, elevated and strategic locations. This is significant both for protection and for being closer to nature and the sky.







Visitors entering the courtyards of the domes encounter an atmosphere of peace, tranquillity and purity that takes them away from the weariness of the outside world. Each dome symbolizes an important event, figure or period in Yazidi history.




A philosophy of purity, light and peace




One of the most distinctive characteristics of Yazidis is their attachment to the colour white.




In the Yazidi faith, white is not merely a style of dress but a deeply sacred symbol representing purity of heart and spirit, light, peace and authenticity.







Wearing white during religious rituals, prayers, visits to the domes and religious ceremonies reflects the unity of the community and the authenticity of the faith. The colour keeps alive in their minds and spirits a direct connection with the sun and light. Although the Yazidi community has endured many Fermans (genocides), hardships and changes throughout history, this culture has preserved its authentic

author: Unknown
title: How can we call them dead?
content:
We were together at a morale event in 2017. A young, graceful woman comrade stepped onto the stage to read a poem. She was very short and endearing. We looked at her with smiles; there was something immediately lovable about her. But her face was deeply serious, and when we saw her expression, our smiles faded too.




She began to read her poem. Its title was How Could We Call Them Dead?




She was reading it in memory of 23 of our loved ones who had been martyred in an air strike on a single day that year. She was giving voice to our pain. Those 23 lives, each one beautiful, each one courageous. With coal-black eyebrows, golden hair, proud foreheads, mischievous ways and chubby cheeks, they were warm, deeply warm comrades. All of them so young. We buried our pain in our hearts, as we had done with so many comrades over the years. Hardest of all was not being able to announce their martyrdom at the time, so that the enemy would not rejoice or take courage and so that the impact of such attacks could be contained. Neither friend nor foe was told. Saying, “Until the day comes,” we carried their pain in our hearts and continued along the path, trying not to fall behind in the marathon to liberate our country. And that endearing yet serious comrade, with features as beautiful as though they had been drawn with a pencil, was offering us something to hold on to. She was giving us t

title: CPT report documents overcrowding, ill-treatment and isolation in Turkish prisons
content:
The Council of Europe’s Committee for the Prevention of Torture (CPT) has published two long-withheld reports on conditions in Turkish prisons and police detention facilities. The findings are based on visits conducted in January 2021 and February 2024. The reports were not made public until October 6, 2026, after the Turkish authorities agreed to their publication. The findings range from severe overcrowding and allegations of physical ill-treatment to years of de facto isolation in high-security prisons. The CPT paid particular attention to prisoners serving aggravated life sentences, as well as women and LGBTIQ+ prisoners.




During its 2021 visit, the delegation inspected 13 police and gendarmerie facilities, including police headquarters and counterterrorism units in Ankara, Diyarbakır and Istanbul. It also visited eight prisons, including women’s prisons in Istanbul-Bakırköy and Kayseri, a juvenile prison in Istanbul-Maltepe and a high-security prison in Diyarbakır.




The special visit in February 2024

 

focused on four high-security prisons in Antalya, Iğdır and Van, as well as two L-type prisons in Antalya and Maltepe, Istanbul. Particular attention was paid to the detention conditions of prisoners serving aggravated life sentences, as well as the situation of women, LGBTIQ+ prisoners and people held in solitary confinement for administrative or disciplinary reason

title: RAJIN on Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day: We will continue the struggle for free press undeterred
content:
The coordination of the Free Women’s Press (RAJIN, Ragihandina Azad a Jinan) has commemorated Kurdish journalist and revolutionary Gurbetelli Ersöz on the 29th anniversary of her death. Ersöz was the first woman to serve as editor-in-chief of a newspaper in Turkey. RAJIN paid tribute to her legacy for the free press and the women’s movement and declared that it would continue her struggle amid increasing repression.




Gurbetelli Ersöz was born in 1965 in the village of Akbulut in Elazığ. After studying chemistry at Çukurova University, she completed a master’s degree and worked as a research assistant. She became politically active in 1987 and was imprisoned in 1989. Following her release in 1993, she became editor-in-chief of the newspaper Özgür Gündem.




She was detained along with numerous employees of the newspaper and severely tortured while in police custody. Following another period of imprisonment lasting around six months and amid increasing threats from paramilitary structures, she joined the guerrilla ranks in the mountains of Kurdistan in 1995. There, she also assumed responsibilities within the women’s organization YAJK. On October 8, 1997, Ersöz was caught in an ambush by the KDP and lost her life in the ensuing clash.




“Not gone, but became the path herself”




Twenty-nine years after her death, RAJIN described Ersöz as a trailblazer whose political and j

title: DEM Party: There has been no change in Öcalan’s conditions
content:
The DEM Party calls for concrete steps to further implement the peace and democratic society process. During a meeting with parliamentary correspondents in Ankara on Wednesday, parliamentary group chairs Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit and Sezai Temelli made clear that there has still been no progress, particularly regarding the working and communication conditions of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan.




At the same time, the party calls for the implementation of the framework law that has already been adopted, the commencement of work by parliamentary bodies, and further legal measures to facilitate the return of members of the Kurdish freedom movement and the release of political prisoners.




“Framework law must be implemented in practice”




For the next stage of the process, the DEM Party now sees parliament as bearing primary responsibility. Koçyiğit called on the National Assembly to present a concrete roadmap and set in motion the mechanisms for implementing the framework law that has already been adopted. The establishment of the legal basis must now be followed by practical implementation, she said, warning that further delays could have a direct impact on the process as a whole.




According to the party, the parliamentary structures for the next phase must also begin their work. Temelli referred to the anticipated commission and emphasized that what matters is not so much

author: Unknown
title: Hatimoğulları: What is the National Security Council still waiting for?
content:
DEM Party co-chair Tülay Hatimoğulları has criticized delays in the peace and democratic society process and called for concrete steps. Neither have the envisaged mechanisms been fully set in motion, nor have Abdullah Öcalan’s working and communication conditions fundamentally changed, she stated.




Speaking at an extraordinary party congress in Iğdır province, Hatimoğulları pointed to growing uncertainty over the future course of the process. “What is going to happen? Why is the process not moving forward? What is the National Security Council still waiting for? What are the confirmation and determination still waiting for?” she asked.




Council for Disarmament and Strategic Coordination has not yet begun its work




At the center of her criticism was the Council for Disarmament and Strategic Coordination envisaged under the framework law. Although there is an understanding regarding Öcalan’s role within this mechanism, it has yet to be activated. “This commission is still not active and has not begun its work. What are they waiting for?” Hatimoğulları said. As a result, key structures intended to move the process into its next phase remain unable to function, she said and called for the necessary steps to be taken without further delay.




“We want to speak with Öcalan”

title: KCDK-E and TJK-E call for Europe-wide actions for Öcalan
content:
The Congress of Democratic Societies of Kurdistan in Europe (KCDK-E) and the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E) have called for actions across Europe to mark the 28th anniversary of the international plot against Abdullah Öcalan. Demonstrations and rallies have been announced in cities including Düsseldorf, Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Bremen, Bern, London, Stockholm, Brussels, Paris and Vienna. The mobilization centers on demands for Öcalan’s physical freedom and for conditions that would enable negotiations and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question to move forward.




The process referred to as the international plot began on October 9, 1998, when Öcalan was forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country. This was followed by a months-long odyssey through various countries, ending on February 15, 1999, with his abduction from the Kenyan capital Nairobi to Turkey. The Kurdish leader has been held on the prison island of Imrali ever since.




Attack on the will of the Kurdish people




KCDK-E and TJK-E described the events beginning on October 9, 1998, as an international intervention directed not only against Öcalan but also against the political achievements and the Kurdish people’s will for freedom. title: ISIS carries out another attack in Hawija
content:
Another attack by the terrorist group Islamic State (ISIS) has taken place within a short period of time in Hawija, southwest of Kirkuk. Late Tuesday evening, ISIS members attacked a base belonging to the 2nd Battalion of the 61st Brigade of the Hashd al-Shaabi. Troops stationed at the base returned fire. No deaths or injuries were reported.




The attack took place in the Bargliya–Danadish area, where an Iraqi Federal Police post had been attacked just one day earlier. Two police officers were killed and several others injured in that attack. Security measures in Hawija were subsequently tightened.




The Federal Police initially announced a nighttime curfew from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. It was later clarified that the curfew applies only to the Danadish sector, which comprises five villages. Freedom of movement remained largely unaffected in other parts of Hawija.

title: YRJ on October 7: Women’s journalism documents struggle and history
content:
On the occasion of Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day on October 7, the Association of Women Journalists in Rojava (YRJ) has commemorated Gurbetelli Ersöz, Dilîşan Îbiş and Dilovan Gever, as well as all those from the free press who lost their lives. “For Kurdish women, journalism is not merely a profession, but a means of documenting history, making social realities visible and carrying women’s voices to the world,” it said.




In a written statement, the YRJ paid tribute to the path forged by Kurdish women journalists through their words, writings and images. Under the most difficult conditions, it said, they documented the truth and brought women’s experiences, struggles and problems in particular into the public sphere.




Tribute to Gurbetelli Ersöz




YRJ attributed particular significance to journalist and guerrilla commander Gurbetelli Ersöz, who lost her life in 1997 during the so-called “Southern War.” The day of her death is observed as Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day. Ersöz is regarded as one of the formative figures of Kurdish women’s journalism. The YRJ recalled that today’s women’s journalism builds on the work and sacrifices of the women journalists who pioneered and continued this path under difficult conditions.




The statement also commemorated Dilîşan Îbiş and Dilovan Gever. Îbiş lost her life on October 12, 2017, and Gever on October 13, 2019. Both document

title: Geothermal development threatens villages in the Zilan Valley
content:
In the Zilan Valley near Erciş district in the province of Van, the conflict over geothermal development in the region is intensifying. The villages of Şorik (İkizçalı), Karakilise (İşbaşı) and Çaxirbeg (Çakırbey) see their living environment threatened by the expansion of the projects. Residents report that the possible evacuation of the villages is now also being discussed and that signatures are being collected.




According to the information available so far, no official evacuation order has been issued. However, work sites and drilling areas have already been established in Karakilise and Çaxirbeg. The projects are therefore directly encroaching on residential areas, agricultural land and the livelihoods of the local population.




The conflict is not new. State-backed geothermal development in the Zilan Valley has been underway since at least 2020. Since then, drilling operations, further planning and large-scale tenders for the exploitation of geothermal resources have followed.







Project launched in 2020




At the end of November 2020, the Eastern Anatolia Development Agency (DAKA) and the Van Governor’s Office signed an agreement for a project to develop geothermal resources for agricultural use in Erciş. The project was part of the Turkish Ministry of Industry and Technology’s support program for so-called attraction centers.

author: Unknown
title: Artist Cesim Başboğa sentenced to 10 months in prison
content:
Artist Cesim Başboğa was prosecuted over songs he performed at the Culture and Arts Festival held in Tatvan (Tetwan), Bitlis (Bedlîs), in 2025.




The songs Serhildan Jiyan e, Lê Amedê and Zana û Andok, which Başboğa performed at the festival, were cited as evidence in the case brought against him on allegations of “making propaganda for an organization.”




At the second hearing of the case, held today at the Bitlis 2nd High Criminal Court, the court sentenced Başboğa to 10 months in prison.




Başboğa said in his defence that, at a time when peace is being discussed, imposing sentences on artists who perform music in their mother tongue harms the process.

title: Karasu: Democratization is for everyone
content:
KCK Executive Council member Mustafa Karasu discussed developments in Kurdistan, Turkey, and the Middle East during a special program on 

Medya Haber

.




Referring to the ongoing “Peace and Democratic Society” process, Karasu noted that the movement had taken the necessary steps, but that the Turkish state was still resisting. He said that a century-old problem such as the Kurdish issue could not be resolved through old laws, an outdated legal framework, or an old political approach.




Reminding that the existing laws had failed to resolve the issue, leading to decades of conflict, Karasu stressed that new laws guaranteeing freedom must be enacted in order to resolve the problem.




This is the first part of the interview.




Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan sent a message to the Peace and Democratic Integration conference held in London. A notable assessment in this message was that if the republic does not become democratic, democratic integration will not be realized either. How should this be understood?




Now, we speak of democratic integration and unification. The unification of two things: the unification of the Kurdish people with the state and with the Turkish people on a democratic basis. author: Unknown
title: Students in Afrin and Aleppo demand a solution
content:
Although the new academic year began a couple of months ago, the situation of nearly 1,000 students studying in Autonomous Administration schools, as well as the teachers working in these schools, remains uncertain.




Dozens of students attending Autonomous Administration schools held a protest in Efrîn over the continued uncertainty surrounding their situation.




The students said they were being systematically excluded as students from Efrîn and Aleppo, stating that this exclusion ranged from being deprived of education to deficiencies in language instruction.




The statement said that students and teachers had not been included in the integration of social institutions or the education system, and called for steps to be taken as soon as possible.




It was stated that a transition process would be prepared within the framework of the Autonomous Administration’s curriculum for students in the ninth and twelfth grades. However, the statement noted that no action had been taken for the nearly 1,000 students in these two grade levels.




The students demanded that their requests be addressed within two weeks, saying that otherwise they would continue taking to the streets.
